title: pocketone.yaml reference
text: Every section the pocketone binary understands, from pocketone config --json . Each plugin owns its own section. pocketone config check checks a file. How the file works (where it's found, .env secrets) is on the Config page.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: app:
text: The single app: data dir, dev mode, encryption, hooks, migrations, public dir, and the .env names it may read (env_allow). Not used when a provider runs many instances. dir string The data folder (pb_data). Default: pb_data next to the executable. The --dir flag wins. dev bool Dev mode: logs and SQL statements printed to the console. The --dev flag wins. encryption_env string Name of the environment variable holding a 32-character key that encrypts the app settings. The --encryptionEnv flag wins. query_timeout duration Default timeout for SELECT queries, such as 30s. The --queryTimeout flag wins. hooks_dir string The JS hooks folder. Default: pb_hooks next to pb_data. The --hooksDir flag wins. hooks_watch bool Restart the app when a pb_hooks file changes. On unless false. The --hooksWatch flag wins. hooks_pool int How many JS runtimes are kept ready for hooks. Default 15. The --hooksPool flag wins. migrations_dir string The migrations folder. Default: pb_migrations next to pb_data. The --migrationsDir flag wins. automigrate bool Write a migration file when you change collections in the dashboard. On unless false. The --automigrate flag wins. public_dir string The static files folder. Default: pb_public next to the executable. The --publicDir flag wins. index_fallback bool Serve index.html for a missing static path, for single-page apps. On unless false. The --indexFallback flag wins. env_allow list of string Names from the .env the app and its JS hooks may read. Default none.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: autotls:
text: Automatic HTTPS certificates (ACME): auto, email, CA, domains, DNS-01, certificate storage. The --autotls flags win. auto bool Get certificates through ACME (CertMagic). Flag: --autotls. email string ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. Flag: --autotlsEmail. ca string letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL. Flag: --autotlsCA. storage string Where certificates are kept. Default pb_data/.autotls. domains list of string Extra domains to get at start; wildcards ( .example.com) need dns. Flag: --autotlsDomains. dns.provider string DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges (needed for wildcards): cloudflare. Flag: --autotlsDNS. dns.api_token string The provider's API token. Write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file. dns.api_token_env string Or: the environment variable holding the token. Default CF_API_TOKEN. Flag: --autotlsDNSTokenEnv. Owned by Auto TLS.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: docker:
text: Runtime provider docker: each instance in its own container with the PocketBase (pb:) or PocketOne (p1:) binary of its version (image, binary cache and manifest, instance root, default version, idle stop, limits). socket string The Docker socket. Default $DOCKER_HOST when it is unix://, else /var/run/docker.sock. image string Base image the binaries run in, such as alpine:3.20. Required; pulled when missing. binaries string Folder of the release binary cache and its releases.json. Required. versions list of string The minors this host serves, such as pb:0.36 or p1:0.0 (latest patch of each, from docker update). root string Folder with one folder per instance ( / ). Required. home string The instance folder inside the container. Default /home/pockethost. default_version string Version for instances that name none, such as p1:0.0. . Empty: such instances fail. min_upstream string Oldest upstream PocketBase release served. Default 0.23.0; lower it only for releases you cache yourself. idle_ttl duration Stop a container after this long without requests. Default 10m. max_concurrent_starts int Containers starting at once. Default 4. start_timeout duration How long a container gets to answer its health check. Default 60s. nano_cpus int CPU limit per container in billionths of a CPU (1000000000 = one CPU). 0: no limit. pids_limit int Process limit per container. 0: Docker's default. nofile list of int Open-file limit per container: [soft, hard]. Empty: Docker's default. cap_drop list of string Linux capabilities to drop, such as [ALL]. no_new_privileges bool Set no-new-privileges on every container. network string Docker network for the containers. Default the bridge. adopt_image string Also adopt running unlabeled containers of this image named after an instance id (taking over from another manager). Owned by Docker.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: edges:
text: The fleet: this edge's id and a fixed list of the other edges (id, internal_url, region). self string This edge's id, such as lax-1. list list of object The other edges: id, internal_url (where this edge reaches it) and optional region. Owned by Edge.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: firewall:
text: Peers allowed to connect, trusted proxies and client-IP headers, trusted clients, the rate-limit header prefix. Turns the firewall on. allow_cidrs list of string Peers (IPs or CIDRs) allowed to connect; others get 403. Empty: everyone. trusted_proxies list of string Peers whose client-IP headers are believed. client_ip_headers list of string Headers read, in order, for the client IP from a trusted proxy. Default CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP. trusted_clients list of string Client IPs or CIDRs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance. trusted_client_headers list of string Headers a trusted client uses to name its end user's IP, so each user gets their own limits. Default X-Client-IP. rate_limit_header_prefix string Prefix of the rate-limit response headers. Default X-RateLimit. Owned by Firewall.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: instances:
text: Where a multi-instance host's instances come from (a YAML file), and dev mode (serve unknown hostnames). file string instances.yaml The instances file (id, hosts and settings for each instance), reloaded when it changes. dev bool Also serve unknown hostnames: each becomes an instance named after it, in dev mode, with its folder made on first use. Owned by Host.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: lifecycle:
text: Instance data on this host: how often disk use is measured and last-request times are reported. measure_every duration 24h0m0s How old an instance's disk measurement may get before it is measured again. Default 24h. report_every duration 1h0m0s How often changed last-request times are reported to the sink. Default 1h. concurrency int 2 How many instances are measured at once. Default 2. Owned by Lifecycle.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: mothership:
text: A community mothership to mirror instances and edges from: url, login, this edge's id, internal URL, region, apex. url string The mothership's URL. Required. email string Superuser email this edge logs in with; use a $VAR from the .env. password string Superuser password; use a $VAR from the .env. self string This edge's edge_id, such as lax-1. Default: the edges section's self. Required. internal_url string Where other edges reach this one. Set: the edge registers itself when the mothership has no record for it. region string Region recorded when the edge registers itself. apex string Makes . a hostname of every instance. Empty: hosts only. heartbeat duration How often this edge marks itself online. Default 15s; negative: never. resync duration How often everything is reloaded, in case a change was missed. Default 10m. Owned by Mothership.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: pitr:
text: Point-in-time restore: on by default, retention, snapshot interval. The --pitr and --pitrRetention flags win. enabled bool On unless false. The --pitr flag wins. retention duration How far back a restore can go. Default 72h. The --pitrRetention flag wins. snapshot_interval duration How often a full copy is taken. Default 24h. Shorter: faster restores, more storage. Owned by PITR.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: pocker:
text: Runtime provider pocker: instances run in-process (root folder, hooks pool, egress allow list, instance limit defaults). root string ./pb_root The folder holding one folder per instance: / . hooks_pool_size int 2 JS runtimes kept ready per instance (0: a new one for each hook run). max_js_execution duration 30s Longest any single JS call (hook, route, cron job, migration) may run. max_js_allocation int 67108864 Largest result a JS built-in may allocate in one step, such as 64MiB. max_call_stack_size int 2000 Deepest JS recursion allowed. max_sleep duration 10s Longest a JS sleep() call may wait. max_query_duration duration 30s Longest an SQL statement without its own deadline may run. http_send_max_timeout duration 1m0s Longest timeout a JS $http.send call may use. http_send_max_body int 10485760 Largest response body a JS $http.send call may read, such as 10MiB. max_concurrent_js int 16 JS calls an instance runs at once; more wait up to max_js_execution, then fail. egress_allow list of string Private networks (CIDRs) instances may still connect to. Default none: public addresses only. Owned by Pocker.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: provider:
text: The runtime provider that runs many instances (pocker or docker). Omit for a single stock app.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: rate_limits:
text: Default rate limits for every instance (per instance: plugins.firewall.rate_limits). Turns the firewall on. ip_hourly int Requests per hour from one client IP to one instance. Default 1000. instance_hourly int Requests per hour to one instance from everyone. Default 10000. ip_concurrent int Requests one client IP may have open on one instance at once. Default 15. instance_concurrent int Requests one instance may have open at once. Default 250. file_weight number What a /api/files request costs, as a share of a request. Default 0.1. trusted.ip_hourly int Requests per hour from one trusted client IP to one instance. trusted.instance_hourly int Requests per hour to one instance. trusted.ip_concurrent int Requests one trusted client IP may have open on one instance at once. trusted.instance_concurrent int Requests one instance may have open at once. off bool No rate limiting. The default in dev mode unless rate_limits is set. Owned by Firewall.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: s3redirect:
text: Signed S3 redirects for file downloads: enabled, URL lifetime. The --s3Redirect and --s3RedirectTTL flags win. enabled bool On unless false (it only acts when S3 file storage is on). Flag: --s3Redirect. ttl duration How long each signed URL stays valid. Default 5m, max 7 days. Flag: --s3RedirectTTL. Owned by S3 Redirect.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: server:
text: How the binary listens: http, https and CORS origins (single-app mode: the serve command's defaults). http string Plain HTTP address, such as 127.0.0.1:8090. Single app: the --http default (the flag wins). Many instances: redirects to https when https is set. https string HTTPS address. Single app: the --https default (the flag wins). Many instances: the main address. origins list of string Allowed CORS origins. Single app: the --origins default (the flag wins). plain list of string Many instances only: extra plain HTTP addresses with no redirect. tls.cert string Many instances only: the certificate file, reloaded when it changes. tls.key string Many instances only: the private key file, reloaded when it changes. shutdown_timeout duration Many instances only: how long in-flight requests get to finish at stop.

title: Installation
text: PocketOne is one executable, pocketone . It is built on PocketBase v0.41 and takes the same commands and flags, plus its own.

title: Installation
heading: Homebrew (macOS and Linux)
text: brew install pockethost/tap/pocketone The formula lives in pockethost/homebrew-tap.

title: Installation
heading: Download a release
text: Download the zip for your platform from Releases, unzip it, and put pocketone somewhere on your PATH .

title: Installation
heading: Build from source
text: With Go installed: git clone https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone.git cd pocketone/examples/pocketone go build -o pocketone .

title: Installation
heading: Run it
text: pocketone serve Open http://127.0.0.1:8090/_/ to create your first superuser, as in PocketBase. To start a site with server-rendered pages: pocketone pages create myapp cd myapp pocketone serve --dev --dir ./pb_data In dev mode ( serve --dev ), an app with no SMTP settings doesn't send mail through the system's sendmail . PocketOne catches the mail and shows it at http://127.0.0.1:8025 .

title: Installation
heading: Upgrade
text: pocketone upgrade This replaces the executable with the latest release. The old one is kept beside it as pocketone- , never deleted, so you can go back.

title: Installation
heading: Moving from PocketBase
text: PocketOne reads the same pb_data , pb_hooks , pb_migrations and pb_public folders. Point it at your existing data directory with --dir , as you would with pocketbase . Back up pb_data first.

title: What is PocketOne?
text: PocketOne is a community fork of PocketBase. It tracks upstream PocketBase and keeps its own changes to the core small: only the hooks that let plugins extend and override PocketBase. Every feature lives in a plugin. It's maintained by PocketHost, which runs it in production. PocketOne is not affiliated with or endorsed by the PocketBase project.

title: What is PocketOne?
heading: How it's built
text: A small core. PocketBase's own code changes only to add hooks. Each change is marked in the source, reviewed by someone who didn't write it, and kept minimal so upstream releases merge cleanly. Everything else is a plugin. Plugins live in ext/ in the repo. Each is its own Go module, with a README and a small example. Off until you use it. The plugins in the pocketone binary add no work to an app that doesn't use them. One app or hundreds. A plugin written against the plugin contract works the same on a single app and on every instance under a multi-instance host.

title: What is PocketOne?
heading: Open to contributions
text: PocketOne is open to everyone. Ask questions and share ideas in GitHub Discussions, report bugs in Issues, and send plugins as pull requests. Start with Writing a plugin.

text: Install PocketOne See what PocketOne adds to PocketBase Browse the plugins

title: Auto TLS
text: Automatic HTTPS certificates through ACME, with CertMagic (Caddy's certificate engine). PocketBase already gets Let's Encrypt certificates for serve example.com . Auto TLS takes over that job and adds other certificate authorities, extra domains and wildcard certificates. Status: stable under pocker, beta on a single app. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Auto TLS
heading: Install
text: Auto TLS is built into pocketone and off by default . Turn it on with --autotls (or auto: true in pocketone.yaml ). It only does something when the app serves HTTPS, that is with serve or --https ; on plain HTTP it stays idle, and without it PocketBase's own certificates are used as before. In your own Go build, register it before the app starts: import ( "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/autotls" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pluginkit" ) app := pocketbase.New() pluginkit.MustRegister(app, autotls.NewApp(autotls.Config{Auto: true, Email: "ops@example.com"})) app.Start()

title: Auto TLS
heading: Command-line flags
text: pocketone serve example.com --autotls --autotlsEmail ops@example.com pocketone serve example.com --autotls --autotlsDomains " .example.com" --autotlsDNS cloudflare # token in $CF_API_TOKEN --autotls false Turn it on. --autotlsEmail ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. --autotlsCA letsencrypt letsencrypt , letsencrypt-staging , zerossl , or an ACME directory URL. --autotlsDomains Extra domains, obtained at start (comma separated). Wildcards need --autotlsDNS . --autotlsDNS DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges. Only cloudflare is supported. --autotlsDNSTokenEnv CF_API_TOKEN Environment variable holding the DNS provider's API token.

title: Auto TLS
heading: pocketone.yaml
text: The autotls section sets the defaults for those flags. Flags win over the file. autotls: auto: true email: ops@example.com ca: letsencrypt domains: [" .example.com"] # wildcards need dns dns: provider: cloudflare api_token: $CF_API_TOKEN # read from the .env beside pocketone.yaml storage is only in the file: where certificates are kept (default pb_data/.autotls ). The DNS token can be given as api_token (write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file) or through api_token_env , the name of an environment variable. api_token is only used when --autotlsDNS names the same provider as the file. The Cloudflare token needs permission to edit the zone's DNS. There are no dashboard settings.

title: Auto TLS
heading: autotls:
text: Automatic HTTPS certificates (ACME): auto, email, CA, domains, DNS-01, certificate storage. The --autotls flags win. auto bool Get certificates through ACME (CertMagic). Flag: --autotls. email string ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. Flag: --autotlsEmail. ca string letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL. Flag: --autotlsCA. storage string Where certificates are kept. Default pb_data/.autotls. domains list of string Extra domains to get at start; wildcards ( .example.com) need dns. Flag: --autotlsDomains. dns.provider string DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges (needed for wildcards): cloudflare. Flag: --autotlsDNS. dns.api_token string The provider's API token. Write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file. dns.api_token_env string Or: the environment variable holding the token. Default CF_API_TOKEN. Flag: --autotlsDNSTokenEnv.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Use
text: Once on, there's nothing to click. Start the app as usual with serve (or --https ): Which hostnames get a certificate. The domains given to serve and their www. variants, issued on the first request for each, plus --autotlsDomains , obtained at start. Any other hostname is refused at the TLS handshake, so a random Host can't trigger issuance. How they're proved. TLS-ALPN-01 on the HTTPS port, or DNS-01 when a DNS provider is set (needed for wildcards). HTTP-01 isn't used on a single app, because port 80 is PocketBase's redirect server. Renewal is automatic. Where they're stored. pb_data/.autotls by default, separate from PocketBase's own .autocert_cache . Settings are checked at start, before anything touches the network. A wildcard domain without a DNS provider, a Cloudflare provider without a token, or an unknown provider stops the app with an error such as: tls.domains: wildcard " .example.com" needs a DNS provider (tls.dns); per-hostname certificates work without one With debug logging, the start shows autotls: CertMagic serves HTTPS certificates with the CA and extra domains. Use --autotlsCA letsencrypt-staging while testing, so failed attempts don't count against Let's Encrypt's rate limits.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Pocker
text: Under pocker, the stock pocketone binary (with provider: pocker ) runs autotls.New() , a server plugin that gets certificates for every instance the host serves. It's configured by the same autotls section: autotls: auto: true email: ops@example.com storage: ./pb_root/.pocker-certs # default: .pocker-certs in the pocker root domains: [" .example.com", "example.com"] dns: { provider: cloudflare, api_token_env: CF_API_TOKEN } # only needed for wildcards Without dns , every hostname the instance source maps gets its own certificate on its first TLS handshake, with any DNS host and no API token. Hostnames no instance serves never trigger issuance. Challenges include HTTP-01 on the pocker server's port 80, as well as TLS-ALPN-01 and DNS-01. Certificate files ( server.tls.cert / key ) stay a core pocker feature. Setting both files and auto is an error. Certificates belong to the pocker server, not to instances; the single-app plugin ( NewApp ) is a separate type so it never runs per instance.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Building on Auto TLS
text: autotls.New() implements pocker's Configurer and TLSProvider . A host that builds its own pocker.Server adds it to Plugins : srv := &pocker.Server{Config: cfg, Plugins: []pocker.Plugin{autotls.New()}} AutoTLS.Config can be set in Go before the server starts; the autotls section is read only when Auto is false there. autotls.SupportedDNSProviders lists the dns.provider values it understands.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Example
text: Auto TLS is built into pocketone : examples/pocketone/main.go registers it with the other default plugins.

title: Auto TLS
heading: How it works
text: Go module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/autotls . On a single app, an OnServe hook swaps the TLS config of PocketBase's HTTPS server for CertMagic's. PocketBase's own host policy (the serve domains and www. ) decides which on-demand hostnames are allowed. The certificate manager stops when the app terminates. TLS 1.2 is the minimum; h2 and http/1.1 are offered, and acme-tls/1 stays on for TLS-ALPN challenges. A wildcard in domains covers one level ( .example.com covers a.example.com , not a.b.example.com ).

title: Bulk Mail
text: Campaigns to your app's own users, from the dashboard. You pick who gets the mail with a collection, a view or SQL, write the message, and Bulk Mail sends it at a steady pace through your app's mail settings. It adds one-click unsubscribe, keeps a list of addresses that must never be mailed again, and handles bounces and spam complaints. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Install
text: Bulk Mail is built into pocketone and on for every app. Nothing is sent until a superuser starts a campaign. In your own Go build, register the plugin before the app starts. Bind it into the JS runtime too if you want $bulkmail in pb_hooks : mail := bulkmail.New(bulkmail.Config{Rate: 5, Daily: 5000}) app := pocketbase.New() pluginkit.MustRegister(app, mail) jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{OnInit: func(vm goja.Runtime) { pluginkit.BindJS(app, vm, mail) }}) app.Start() The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bulkmail .

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Configure
text: There is no pocketone.yaml section or command-line flag. The limits are fixed in the binary; pocketone uses the defaults: Per second 5 The most messages this app sends per second. A campaign can only lower it. Per day 5,000 The most messages this app sends per UTC day, across all campaigns. In a custom build, set them with bulkmail.Config{Rate, Daily} . Daily: bulkmail.NoBulkMail forbids sending; the screens then say so.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Settings → Mail
text: Campaigns send through the app's own mail settings and from its sender, both set on Settings → Mail . Below that form there's a Bulk mail section: Postal address : shown in every campaign footer. Anti-spam laws require one. Unsubscribe mailbox : optional. Adds a mailto: alternative to the List-Unsubscribe header. Bounces and complaints (click to open): Amazon SES (SNS) endpoint : the URL to subscribe to the SNS topic your SES identity sends bounce and complaint notifications to. Allowed SNS topic ARNs : comma separated. Empty accepts any topic with a valid AWS signature. Generic webhook and Webhook secret : for other providers. The webhook is off until you set a secret. The section also shows this app's limits and how many messages it sent today. Click Save bulk mail settings . Unsubscribe links and the feedback URLs are built from Settings → Application → Application URL , so set it to the address people reach your app on. The settings are stored in the app's database (a _params row), so they go along with its backups. Secrets are never shown again after saving.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Use
text: The dashboard gets a Mail link in its menu, with two pages: Campaigns and Suppressions . Only superusers see them.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Write a campaign
text: Open Mail and click New campaign . It starts as a draft for verified users of users . Fill in Name , Subject and Body . Under Audience , choose who gets it: Filter : a Collection (or a view), an optional Filter in the same syntax as API rules, and the Email field that holds the address (an email or text field, or a view's computed column). SQL : a read-only SELECT that returns an email column. Every other column is available to the message. Click Count recipients to see how many match, how many are suppressed, and a few sample addresses. Optional: Vars (JSON) for values used in the message, a Schedule (UTC) , and Max per second to send slower than the app's limit. Click Save changes . Preview shows the message for one recipient; Send test mails it to the Test address . A view is the easy way to build a dynamic audience: it picks who gets mail and computes the columns the message uses. The example creates one called newsletter_audience .

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Placeholders
text: In the subject and body: {{record.field}} : a field or column of the recipient's row, for example {{record.name}} . {{email}} , {{campaign.name}} and {{unsubscribe_url}} . Campaign vars: {"promo": "X"} gives {{promo}} . A var can be computed once when sending starts: {"count": {"sql": "SELECT COUNT( ) AS value FROM users"}} . {{if record.field}}…{{else}}…{{end}} blocks, and {{if !record.field}} for the opposite. Values are HTML-escaped in the body. An unsubscribe footer with your postal address is always added.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Send
text: Click Send (or Schedule when a time is set) and confirm. The campaign page shows its status and progress (sent, queued, skipped, failed), and a Recipients table you can filter by status. While it runs you can Pause , Resume or Cancel it. Every address is queued once per campaign. Sending a finished campaign again mails only new matches. A message counts as sent only once the mail server accepts it, so a restart doesn't send twice or skip anyone. A permanent error (SMTP 5xx) fails that recipient. Other errors are retried, up to three attempts. A campaign pauses itself when more than 5% of its sends fail after the first 100, or when spam complaints pass 0.3% of its sends (at least 3). The reason shows next to its status.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Suppressions
text: Mail → Suppressions lists the addresses that never receive campaign mail, whatever the audience says. Unsubscribes, permanent bounces and complaints are added automatically. Click Add address to add one by hand, a row to edit or delete it, or Export CSV to download the list.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Unsubscribing
text: Every message has a signed unsubscribe link and the List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post: One-Click headers that Gmail and Yahoo require for bulk senders. Opening the link shows a confirm button, so link scanners can't unsubscribe anyone. The one-click request from a mail provider unsubscribes directly.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Try it locally
text: In dev mode with SMTP off, pocketone catches every mail, bulk mail included, in an inbox at http://127.0.0.1:8025: pocketone serve --dev

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Works with
text: Pocker Add the same plugin value to srv.Plugins and every instance gets Bulk Mail. Each instance can override its limits (below). $bulkmail only reaches the instance's own data, so it's safe for untrusted tenants. Mailtrap In dev mode with SMTP off, campaign mail lands in the local inbox instead of being sent.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Per-instance settings (pocker)
text: Each instance's plugins.bulkmail settings apply over the Config given to bulkmail.New : instances: id: abc plugins: { bulkmail: { rate: 2, daily: 1000 } } id: free-plan-app plugins: { bulkmail: { daily: 0 } } # may not send bulk mail id: other plugins: { bulkmail: { enabled: false } } # no Bulk Mail at all

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Go API
text: bulkmail.For(app) returns the app's service: Start , StartLimit , Pause , Resume , Cancel , Preview , Test , CountAudience , Suppress , Unsuppress , IsSuppressed , Unsubscribe , UnsubscribeURL , Limits , and the hooks: OnSend fires before every campaign message (not test sends). Change the message, or return an error to fail that recipient. OnUnsubscribe fires when someone unsubscribes through a link or the one-click header. OnFeedback fires for each bounce or complaint a provider reports. Config.Mailer swaps the mail client, for example for a platform relay. Config.PublicURL sets the base of unsubscribe links instead of the Application URL.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: JS API
text: $bulkmail in pb_hooks : $bulkmail.start(id, [limit]) // limit: queue only the next N new recipients $bulkmail.pause(id); $bulkmail.resume(id); $bulkmail.cancel(id) $bulkmail.test(id, [to]); $bulkmail.preview(id, [email]) $bulkmail.count({collection, filter, email_field} {sql}) // {count, suppressed, sample} $bulkmail.suppress(email, [reason]); $bulkmail.unsuppress(email); $bulkmail.isSuppressed(email) $bulkmail.unsubscribe(email, [campaignId]); $bulkmail.unsubscribeURL(email, [campaignId]) $bulkmail.limits() // {rate, daily, sentToday} React to activity with record hooks on the collections below, for example onRecordAfterCreateSuccess((e) = { … }, "_bulkmail_suppressions") .

title: Bulk Mail
heading: REST API
text: Superusers only: GET / PATCH /api/bulkmail/settings Settings (secrets are never returned), limits and feedback endpoint URLs. POST /api/bulkmail/audience/count {"audience": {...}} → count, suppressed, sample. POST /api/bulkmail/campaigns/{id}/start\ pause\ resume\ cancel Campaign actions. start takes an optional {"limit": N} to queue only the next N new recipients. POST /api/bulkmail/campaigns/{id}/preview The rendered message for one recipient. POST /api/bulkmail/campaigns/{id}/test Send to test_to (no ledger rows). Campaigns and suppressions are created and edited through the regular records API. A campaign's from_name and from_address override the app's sender, but only through the records API, JS or Go (the dashboard doesn't show them), since the app's mail account can usually send only as identities it has verified. Public routes: GET / POST /api/bulkmail/unsubscribe?t=… , POST /api/bulkmail/feedback/ses and POST /api/bulkmail/feedback/webhook . The webhook takes {"type": "bounce complaint unsubscribe", "email": "…"} with an X-Bulkmail-Secret header.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Example
text: example/main.go runs one app with bulk mail: the Mail page, campaigns to the app's own users and $bulkmail in JS hooks. Run it with go run ./example serve --dev from this folder; the dev mail trap at http://127.0.0.1:8025 catches every mail. // Command example runs one PocketBase app with bulk mail: a "Mail" page in the dashboard, campaigns to the app's // own users, and $bulkmail in JS hooks. // // Run it in dev mode: while SMTP is off, PocketOne's dev mail trap catches every mail (bulk mail included) and // shows it at http://127.0.0.1:8025, with nothing else to install: // // go run ./example serve --dev // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/plugins/jsvm" "github.com/dop251/goja" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bulkmail" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pluginkit" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" registerDemoView(app) // a "newsletter_audience" view to use as a campaign audience (demo.go) // the same plugin value pocker would host on every instance (srv.Plugins = append(srv.Plugins, mail)) mail := bulkmail.New(bulkmail.Config{ Rate: 5, // messages per second Daily: 5000, // messages per day; bulkmail.NoBulkMail forbids sending }) pluginkit.MustRegister(app, mail) jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{ OnInit: func(vm goja.Runtime) { pluginkit.BindJS(app, vm, mail) }, // $bulkmail in JS hooks }) if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Bulk Mail
heading: How it works
text: Go module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/bulkmail , a pluginkit plugin. example/main.go runs one app with Bulk Mail ( go run ./example serve --dev ). The audience is resolved when sending starts and queued into a ledger first (one row per campaign and address, unique). A background sender then mails one message at a time through the app's mail client, at the lower of the app's rate and the campaign's. SQL audiences and SQL vars run with SQLite's query_only on, inside a transaction that is always rolled back. Unsubscribe links are signed with HMAC and a per-app secret, generated on first use. SES feedback: SNS signatures are verified, and signing certificates are fetched only from sns. .amazonaws.com . Permanent bounces and complaints go on the suppression list.

title: Bulk Mail
heading: Data
text: _bulkmail_campaigns Content, audience, vars, status, counters, schedule. _bulkmail_sends The ledger: campaign, email, status ( queued , sent , skipped , failed ), reason, attempts. _bulkmail_suppressions Addresses that never receive campaign mail, with the reason. All are superuser-only system collections with fixed collection and field ids ( schema.go ). LegacyJSMigration() emits a PocketBase JS migration that creates the same collections, for apps that move onto this schema before they run this plugin.

title: Config
text: PocketOne's config file: pocketone.yaml , with secrets in a .env beside it. Put your app's settings in one file instead of a long line of flags. Each plugin has its own section in the file. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Config
heading: Install
text: Config is built into pocketone and always on. Without a pocketone.yaml , nothing changes: every setting keeps its default and the flags work as usual. In your own Go build, load the file before the app is created, so its values can be the flags' defaults: cfg, err := config.Load(config.FromArgs(os.Args[1:])) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } appCfg, _ := config.App.Get() app := pocketbase.NewWithConfig(pocketbase.Config{DefaultDataDir: cfg.ResolvePath(appCfg.Dir)}) app.RootCmd.AddCommand(config.NewCommand(func() config.Options { return config.FromArgs(os.Args[1:]) })) The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/config . examples/pocketone/main.go shows the full wiring: every app key as a flag default, and the server keys as the serve command's defaults.

title: Config
heading: Where the files are
text: pocketone.yaml is looked for in the working directory, then next to the executable. --config picks another file. The .env is looked for beside the config file (or in the working directory when there is no config file). --env-file picks another one. Relative paths in the file are relative to the file's folder, so it works from any working directory.

title: Config
heading: What goes in it
text: Each top-level key is one section, owned by the plugin that uses it. This package owns three: server : how the app listens. http , https and origins are the defaults for serve --http , --https and --origins . app : your app's folders and options: the same settings as the root flags ( --dir , --dev , --hooksDir , --publicDir and the rest), plus env_allow . provider : set it only to run many instances from one binary (see Integrations). server: http: 127.0.0.1:8090 origins: [" "] app: dir: ./pb_data hooks_dir: ./pb_hooks env_allow: [STRIPE_KEY] pitr: retention: 168h Other plugins' sections (such as pitr above) are described on their own pages. pocketone config lists every section your binary knows.

title: Config
heading: Flags win
text: A flag on the command line always wins over the file. The file only changes the defaults.

title: Config
heading: Secrets in the .env
text: Write $VAR or ${VAR} in any value, and keep the secret in the .env : autotls: dns: api_token: $CF_API_TOKEN # .env CF_API_TOKEN=abc123 A name is looked up in the .env first, then in the process environment. $$ is a literal $ . A name that is set nowhere stops the app at startup, with the missing names listed. The .env takes KEY=VALUE lines. Blank lines, # comments and an export prefix are fine. Quote a value to keep its spaces; double quotes also understand \n , \t , \" and \\ . The .env is used only for these references. It is never put in the process environment, so your JS hooks ( $os.getenv ) don't see it, unless you list a name in app.env_allow .

title: Config
heading: app:
text: The single app: data dir, dev mode, encryption, hooks, migrations, public dir, and the .env names it may read (env_allow). Not used when a provider runs many instances. dir string The data folder (pb_data). Default: pb_data next to the executable. The --dir flag wins. dev bool Dev mode: logs and SQL statements printed to the console. The --dev flag wins. encryption_env string Name of the environment variable holding a 32-character key that encrypts the app settings. The --encryptionEnv flag wins. query_timeout duration Default timeout for SELECT queries, such as 30s. The --queryTimeout flag wins. hooks_dir string The JS hooks folder. Default: pb_hooks next to pb_data. The --hooksDir flag wins. hooks_watch bool Restart the app when a pb_hooks file changes. On unless false. The --hooksWatch flag wins. hooks_pool int How many JS runtimes are kept ready for hooks. Default 15. The --hooksPool flag wins. migrations_dir string The migrations folder. Default: pb_migrations next to pb_data. The --migrationsDir flag wins. automigrate bool Write a migration file when you change collections in the dashboard. On unless false. The --automigrate flag wins. public_dir string The static files folder. Default: pb_public next to the executable. The --publicDir flag wins. index_fallback bool Serve index.html for a missing static path, for single-page apps. On unless false. The --indexFallback flag wins. env_allow list of string Names from the .env the app and its JS hooks may read. Default none.

title: Config
heading: provider:
text: The runtime provider that runs many instances (pocker or docker). Omit for a single stock app.

title: Config
heading: server:
text: How the binary listens: http, https and CORS origins (single-app mode: the serve command's defaults). http string Plain HTTP address, such as 127.0.0.1:8090. Single app: the --http default (the flag wins). Many instances: redirects to https when https is set. https string HTTPS address. Single app: the --https default (the flag wins). Many instances: the main address. origins list of string Allowed CORS origins. Single app: the --origins default (the flag wins). plain list of string Many instances only: extra plain HTTP addresses with no redirect. tls.cert string Many instances only: the certificate file, reloaded when it changes. tls.key string Many instances only: the private key file, reloaded when it changes. shutdown_timeout duration Many instances only: how long in-flight requests get to finish at stop.

title: Config
heading: See every section
text: pocketone config It prints each section with its description and defaults, as YAML you can copy into your file. For the same list as JSON (each section's name, description, owning plugin, and each key with its type and default): pocketone config --json

title: Config
heading: Check your file
text: pocketone config check It reads the file and the .env and reports problems, or a line like: /srv/app/pocketone.yaml: ok (3 sections), secrets from /srv/app/.env With no file it says no config file: defaults only .

title: Config
heading: What stops startup
text: The app won't start, and says why, when the file has: a top-level key no plugin in the binary owns (usually a typo); the error lists the sections it knows; the same section twice; a value that doesn't fit its key (for example text where a number goes); a $VAR that is set in neither the .env nor the environment. An empty section ( pitr: with nothing after it) is allowed and means all defaults.

title: Config
heading: Works with
text: Every plugin with a section Each plugin declares its own section; its values become that plugin's defaults or flag defaults. PITR, S3 Redirect and Auto TLS are examples. Pocker and Docker Set provider: pocker or provider: docker and pocketone serve runs many instances instead of one app. The app section and env_allow don't apply then; each instance has its own folder under the provider's root.

title: Config
heading: The server section with many instances
text: With a provider, server has a few more keys: https is the main address, http then redirects plain HTTP to it ( http alone serves plain HTTP), plain lists extra plain-HTTP addresses with no redirect, tls names a certificate and key file (reloaded when they change), and shutdown_timeout limits how long in-flight requests get at stop. provider: pocker server: https: ":443" http: ":80" plain: [":8080"] tls: { cert: /etc/certs/cert.pem, key: /etc/certs/key.pem }

title: Config
heading: Give your plugin a section
text: Declare it in your own package with a typed key and defaults: type Config struct { Limit int yaml:"limit" doc:"Requests per minute. The --limit flag wins." } var Section = pluginkit.NewSection("firewall", Config{Limit: 60}, "Request limits for the app.") cfg, found := firewall.Section.Get() // the defaults with the file's values applied cfg, err := firewall.Section.Require() // fails when the file doesn't have the section A plugin reads a section only through its owner's key, so it can read only sections from packages it imports. There is no lookup by name and no access to the raw file. The doc:"…" tag on each field describes the key in pocketone config --json and in the key table on pocketone.dev. config.Load checks every section when the app starts, so a bad value fails early.

title: Config
heading: Example
text: Config is built into pocketone : examples/pocketone/main.go loads pocketone.yaml with it before the app starts and adds the config command.

title: Config
heading: Go API
text: config.FromArgs(args) reads --config and --env-file before the full flag parse. config.Load(opts) finds, reads and checks the files, and makes them the source for every section. config.Read(opts) does the same without checking or installing them. ( Config).ResolvePath(p) makes a relative path from the file absolute, relative to the file's folder. ( Config).AllowEnv(names) copies those .env values into the process environment (what app.env_allow does). config.Describe() returns every section with its keys, types, defaults and docs (the data behind --json ). config.NewCommand(opts) is the config command.

title: Deploy
text: Send your project's code to a running app from your own machine: pb_hooks , pb_migrations , pb_public , packages and the production node_modules tree. Only changed files are uploaded, the app swaps them in and restarts when it needs to. pocketone dev redeploys on every save and streams the app's logs; pull and logs work the other way. pocketone link https://myapp.example.com # add the remote and sign in (Remotes) pocketone deploy # upload what changed pocketone logs Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Deploy
heading: Install
text: Deploy is built into pocketone and on in both directions: every app it serves accepts deploys from its superusers, and the deploy , dev , pull and logs commands are there to deploy to other apps. There's nothing to install. In your own Go build, register it before the app starts. Remotes gives the commands their remotes and logins, and Tokens lets you deploy with API tokens: app := pocketbase.New() tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{}) // optional: API tokens with the deploy scope remotes.MustRegister(app, remotes.Config{}) // remotes, login, and /_pocker/whoami discovery deploy.MustRegister(app, deploy.Config{}) // the deploy API + deploy/dev/pull/logs commands app.Start() The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy . deploy.Config{DisableServer: true} keeps only the commands, for a binary that deploys elsewhere but must not accept deploys.

title: Deploy
heading: Configure
text: There is no pocketone.yaml section, flag or settings screen. Defaults on the receiving app: Who may deploy: superusers. You sign in with pocketone login (see Remotes) or use an API token. A token needs the deploy scope (or no scopes); deploy:read allows reading files and logs only. Where files land: next to pb_data , PocketBase's usual layout ( pb_hooks/ , pb_migrations/ , pb_public/ , node_modules/ beside it). Upload store: uploaded files and past deploys are kept in .pb_deploy/ next to pb_data . It's outside pb_data , so backups skip it, and it's never deployed. On your machine, the commands use the project's remotes and saved logins from Remotes. In CI, set POCKETONE_TOKEN (or POCKETONE_TOKEN_ ) instead of signing in.

title: Deploy
heading: Use
text: All commands take an optional remote name or URL; without one they use the project's default remote. Run them from your project folder (or any folder below it).

title: Deploy
heading: deploy
text: pocketone deploy # to the default remote pocketone deploy prod -m "fix signup" # to the remote "prod", with a note pocketone deploy --dry-run # list what would be sent, send nothing pocketone deploy --out /tmp/set # write the files to a folder instead You'll see how many files are deployed and how many are uploaded, then a line like Deployed : 3 changed, 0 deleted, 41 unchanged. Restarted. With nothing changed it says Up to date: no changes. --dry-run List what would be deployed; deploy nothing. --out Write the deploy set to a local folder instead of deploying. -i , --include Add include patterns to the default set. -e , --exclude Exclude patterns ( pb_data is always excluded). --node-modules Ship the production node_modules tree (the default when there's a package.json ). --no-node-modules Don't ship node_modules ; leave the remote's alone. --commit Commit to record. Default: $GITHUB_SHA , $CI_COMMIT_SHA , or git HEAD . -m , --message A note to record with the deploy. -v , --verbose List every file. What's sent: files matching pb_ and pb_ / / except pb_data , plus package.json , bun.lock(b) and patches/ . Dotfiles are included ( pb_public/.well-known ); .git files and symlinks are skipped. Packages: with a package.json , the production node_modules tree is collected the way Node resolves it (hoisted npm and bun, pnpm's store, workspace links; never devDependencies) and shipped as plain files, so plain JS hooks can require npm packages. The remote then owns its root node_modules : packages you no longer ship are removed there. Restarts: a deploy that changes anything outside pb_public restarts the app about a second after it answers. Files are swapped in while the app runs, each rename atomic. A deploy that only touches pb_public doesn't restart.

title: Deploy
heading: dev
text: pocketone dev Deploys now, then again on every change (half a second after the last save), and streams the remote's logs. --no-logs turns the log stream off. It takes the same file flags as deploy . Stop it with Ctrl+C.

title: Deploy
heading: pull
text: pocketone pull prod # pb_hooks, pb_migrations, pb_public, package.json pocketone pull prod pb_hooks pb_public/index.html pocketone pull prod --dry-run Downloads files from a remote into the project. pb_data is only reachable on an instance that's powered off, so a single app (always running while it answers) refuses it.

title: Deploy
heading: logs
text: pocketone logs prod pocketone logs prod -n 20 Replays the last 100 lines ( -n , --lines , 0 to 1000), then follows. Requests show as GET /url → 200 (1.2 ms) and errors are marked ERR . PocketBase writes its logs in batches, so lines show up a few seconds late. The stream reconnects by itself if it drops.

title: Deploy
heading: Deploy history
text: Every deploy is recorded in the _deploys collection of the receiving app: status, file counts, bytes, commit, message, source, token name, superuser and any error. Superusers can browse it in the dashboard.

title: Deploy
heading: Works with
text: Remotes Gives the commands their remotes, saved logins and CI tokens. The commands find the deploy API through the remote's /_pocker/whoami . OAuth Server pocketone login signs in through the browser when the remote runs it. Tokens Deploy registers the deploy and deploy:read scopes, so you can make API tokens for CI that can only deploy or only read. Pocker The same API runs for many instances with your own backend: build it with deploy.New (below). PocketHost does this. PocketHost A remote without /_pocker/whoami is taken to be a PocketHost instance: the commands use /_ph/deploy/v1 and a PocketHost token ( POCKETHOST_TOKEN , or the pockethost remote read from .pockethostconfig ).

title: Deploy
heading: Building on Deploy
text: Go client. deploy.NewClient(ctx, rc) takes a Remotes client and finds its deploy API. Deploy , Pull , Collect and Watch are the commands' building blocks. Your own host. deploy.New(deploy.Options{Prefix, Backend, Instances, PBRoot, DataRoot, PlatformPaths, Logs}) builds the API; mount api.Wrap(next) . Backend decides which instance a request is for ( Lookup(r) ), who it acts as ( Authenticate(r, inst) → Auth{UserID, Scopes, Via, TokenLabel} , an AuthError , or ErrNoAccess for a 404) and records history. Instances is pocker's Manager (stop, swap, start). The default FileLogs tails each instance's logs/exec.log , which pocker writes. PocketHost composes it with its own token backend and keeps /_ph/deploy/v1 . Discovery. Deploy advertises itself as the deploy feature of /_pocker/whoami , so clients find its path.

title: Deploy
heading: Example
text: example/main.go is an app that both accepts deploys and makes them: the deploy API, API tokens, remotes and the deploy commands. Its comment walks through a first deploy against itself. // Command example is a PocketBase that accepts deploys and can deploy: the deploy API (/_pocker/deploy/v1), API // tokens, remotes, and the deploy/dev/pull/logs commands. // // go run ./example serve --http=127.0.0.1:8090 # the remote // cd myproject && mkdir pb_hooks && echo 'routerAdd("GET", "/hi", (e) = e.string(200, "hi"))' pb_hooks/main.pb.js // go run ./example link http://127.0.0.1:8090 --email admin@example.com # password: password // go run ./example deploy // curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/hi // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/plugins/jsvm" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // deployed pb_hooks and pb_migrations tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{}) remotes.MustRegister(app, remotes.Config{}) deploy.MustRegister(app, deploy.Config{}) // deploys land next to pb_data if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Deploy
heading: Deploy API
text: /_pocker/deploy/v1 (superusers, see Configure): GET /whoami Who the request acts as, on which instance. POST /check Takes a manifest, returns the hashes the server is missing. POST /blobs Gzipped PHB1 bundles: [sha256][uint32 length][bytes] …, every hash verified, 64 MB per request. POST /commit Stage, swap in, record, restart. GET / DELETE /files List or delete files. GET / PUT /files/raw Download or upload one file. GET /logs The app's logs as server-sent events. The protocol is the pockethost npm CLI's, so the same client deploys to PocketOne apps and PocketHost.

title: Deploy
heading: How it works
text: Go module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy . example/main.go is an app that accepts deploys and can deploy (logins from devusers: admin@example.com / password). A deploy is a hash diff: the client sends a manifest, uploads only the missing files in bundles, then commits. On a single app the files are swapped in while it runs, then app.Restart() re-executes the process ( Config.Restart overrides it; not on Windows). Config.Dir and Config.StoreDir move the deploy folder and the upload store; Config.Prefix moves the API. Logs on a single app come from its own _logs table; entries at error level and above are marked as stderr. The node_modules collector is nodemodules , a port of the npm CLI's.

title: Docker
text: Run every instance on a host in its own container, with the official PocketBase or PocketOne binary of the version the instance asks for. One host can serve PocketBase 0.23 and 0.36 and PocketOne side by side. Docker is one of the two runtime providers of the multi-instance host. The other is Pocker, which runs every instance inside one process. A host runs exactly one of them. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Docker
heading: Install
text: Docker is built into pocketone . It needs a Docker daemon on the same machine; nothing else to install. It's off until pocketone.yaml names it as the provider (below). Then pocketone serve runs the host instead of a single app. In your own Go build, register it as a provider of the host before building the host from the config: host.RegisterProvider(&docker.Provider{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath}) h, err := host.FromConfig(host.Options{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath}) The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/docker . Add docker.NewCommand(...) to your root command for the docker seed and docker update commands.

title: Docker
heading: Configure
text: Set provider: docker and a docker section in pocketone.yaml . Listeners ( server ), instances ( instances ) and the firewall are the host's sections. provider: docker docker: image: alpine:3.20 # base image the binaries run in binaries: /var/lib/pocketbase # release binary cache root: /var/lib/instances # one folder per instance: / versions: ["pb:0.23", "pb:0.36", "p1:0.0"] default_version: "pb:0.36. " idle_ttl: 10m max_concurrent_starts: 4 instances: file: ./instances.yaml image , binaries and root are required. Versions. An instance picks its binary with the prefix of its version : pb: is upstream PocketBase, p1: is PocketOne, no prefix means pb: . versions lists the minors the host serves; the newest cached patch that matches wins. A version that isn't listed gets a clear 503. Upstream PocketBase 0.22 and older are refused unless you lower min_upstream and keep those releases in the cache yourself. Per instance ( instances.yaml or a mothership): version , secrets (passed as environment), encryption_key , dev , and dir to put its folder somewhere other than / . An instance with runtime set to anything but docker isn't served here. Limits and hardening are optional: nano_cpus , pids_limit , nofile , cap_drop and no_new_privileges .

title: Docker
heading: docker:
text: Runtime provider docker: each instance in its own container with the PocketBase (pb:) or PocketOne (p1:) binary of its version (image, binary cache and manifest, instance root, default version, idle stop, limits). socket string The Docker socket. Default $DOCKER_HOST when it is unix://, else /var/run/docker.sock. image string Base image the binaries run in, such as alpine:3.20. Required; pulled when missing. binaries string Folder of the release binary cache and its releases.json. Required. versions list of string The minors this host serves, such as pb:0.36 or p1:0.0 (latest patch of each, from docker update). root string Folder with one folder per instance ( / ). Required. home string The instance folder inside the container. Default /home/pockethost. default_version string Version for instances that name none, such as p1:0.0. . Empty: such instances fail. min_upstream string Oldest upstream PocketBase release served. Default 0.23.0; lower it only for releases you cache yourself. idle_ttl duration Stop a container after this long without requests. Default 10m. max_concurrent_starts int Containers starting at once. Default 4. start_timeout duration How long a container gets to answer its health check. Default 60s. nano_cpus int CPU limit per container in billionths of a CPU (1000000000 = one CPU). 0: no limit. pids_limit int Process limit per container. 0: Docker's default. nofile list of int Open-file limit per container: [soft, hard]. Empty: Docker's default. cap_drop list of string Linux capabilities to drop, such as [ALL]. no_new_privileges bool Set no-new-privileges on every container. network string Docker network for the containers. Default the bridge. adopt_image string Also adopt running unlabeled containers of this image named after an instance id (taking over from another manager).

title: Docker
heading: Fetch the binaries
text: pocketone docker update # find the latest patch of each docker.versions minor, record and download it pocketone docker seed # download whatever is recorded but not in the cache yet update checks upstream PocketBase releases (ganigeorgiev.com, then the archived GitHub) and PocketOne releases on GitHub, verifies each download against the release's checksums.txt, and records the list in the cache's releases.json . Run it when you want new patches. Nothing is downloaded at request time: when the host starts, any listed release missing from the cache is downloaded in the background. The cache layout is / / /pocketbase for PocketBase (PocketHost's existing layout) and /p1/ / /pocketone for PocketOne.

title: Docker
heading: Run the host
text: pocketone serve A container starts on an instance's first request and is ready when /api/health answers. At most max_concurrent_starts start at once. It stops after idle_ttl without requests. It restarts on its next request when what it runs changed (secrets, version, mounts). A change to routing only doesn't restart it. It stops when the instance is deleted or moves to another edge. Containers keep running when the host restarts; the next process adopts them by their labels.

title: Docker
heading: Hooks and migrations
text: A change in an instance's pb_hooks restarts its container. PocketBase's own hooks watcher stays on too, so a hook file that fails to load is logged and skipped instead of stopping the instance. A request that arrives while the instance restarts waits for it instead of failing; one that lost its connection mid-restart is sent once more if it's safe to repeat (GET, HEAD or OPTIONS without a body). Migrations run when a container boots.

title: Docker
heading: Maintenance
text: Instance folders are ordinary folders under root . To work on one while nothing has it open, a host's Go code calls WithInstanceStopped (below); requests for that instance wait up to 30 s, then get a 503 with Retry-After .

title: Docker
heading: Switching provider
text: Docker and Pocker both use / , so switching is a config change. Stop the containers first when leaving docker, since they keep running across a host restart on purpose. Data only moves forward: an instance started on a newer PocketBase than wrote its data is upgraded.

title: Docker
heading: Works with
text: Host Docker is a runtime provider of the host: the host routes by hostname, runs the listeners and gates, and hands each request to docker. Pocker The other provider. A host runs one or the other, over the same instance folders. Edge For a fleet: requests for instances on another edge are forwarded there. Mothership Instances (and their versions) come from a mothership instead of a file. Firewall Rate limits and allow lists in front of every instance.

title: Docker
heading: Building on Docker
text: docker.Provider fields extend the provider from Go: Container adds mounts, environment and labels to each container; Version rewrites an instance's version before the binary is picked; OnLog receives container output (default: the debug log); Versions replaces the versions list (for example a fleet's list from a mothership); MinUpstream replaces min_upstream . Spec (what Container fills in): Binds , Env , Labels , plus Cmd to adjust the command (for example drop a flag an old release lacks) and HealthPath / HealthAnyStatus for the readiness check. VersionsSource : any type with Releases(ctx) decides which releases the host serves, each pinned to its download and sha256. YAMLVersions (the versions key) is the built-in one. Runtime API : docker.New(docker.Config{...}) builds the runtime without the config file. WithInstanceStopped(ctx, id, fn) stops an instance, holds its requests and runs fn on its folder (for deploys and restores); StartInstance starts one now; InstanceDir returns its folder. Release helpers : ParseVersion , Pick / PickMin , LatestPatches , Update and Seed are what the commands use.

title: Docker
heading: Example
text: A minimal docker host: instances from a YAML file, each in its own container, routed by hostname on one listener. With a Docker daemon running, start it from this folder with go run ./example --instances instances.yaml --data ./instances --binaries ./bin --versions pb:0.23,p1:0.0 . // A minimal docker host: instances from a YAML file, each in its own container with the PocketBase version it asks // for, routed by hostname on one listener. // // go run ./example --instances instances.yaml --data ./instances --binaries ./bin --versions pb:0.23,p1:0.0 // // instances.yaml: // // instances: // - { id: blog, hosts: [blog.localhost], version: "pb:0.23. " } // - { id: shop, hosts: [shop.localhost], version: "p1:0.0. " } package main import ( "context" "flag" "log/slog" "os" "os/signal" "strings" "syscall" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/docker" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/host" ) func main() { instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file") data := flag.String("data", "./instances", "folder with one folder per instance") binaries := flag.String("binaries", "./bin", "PocketBase binary cache") versions := flag.String("versions", "pb:0.23,p1:0.0", "minors to serve (latest patch each; fetched at start)") image := flag.String("image", "alpine:3.20", "base image") listen := flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.1:8090", "listen address") flag.Parse() b := &docker.Binaries{Root: binaries} tracked := strings.Split( versions, ",") if err := docker.RunUpdate(context.Background(), os.Stdout, docker.DefaultDiscovery(), b, tracked); err != nil { slog.Error("versions", "error", err) os.Exit(1) } rt, err := docker.New(docker.Config{Image: image, DataRoot: data, Binaries: b, Versions: docker.YAMLVersions{Tracked: tracked, Root: b.Root}}) if err != nil { slog.Error("docker", "error", err) os.Exit(1) } ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) defer stop() h := &host.Host{Source: &host.YAMLSource{Path: instances}, Runtime: rt, Listeners: host.Listeners{Listen: listen}} if err := h.Run(ctx); err != nil { slog.Error("host", "error", err) os.Exit(1) } }

title: Docker
heading: How it works
text: Each instance folder is mounted at /home/pockethost and the binary read-only at /home/pockethost/pocketbase . The container runs ./pocketbase serve --http 0.0.0.0:8090 , plus --dev for dev instances and --encryptionEnv=PB_ENCRYPTION_KEY when the instance has an encryption key. Its secrets are its environment. The port is published on 127.0.0.1 and the host proxies to it. This is the layout PocketHost's Node edge uses, so its instance folders and binary cache move as they are. Every container carries labels: p1.runtime , p1.instance , p1.version (the resolved release, such as pb:0.36.9 ) and p1.spec (a hash of its configuration, used to tell when it must restart). adopt_image also adopts unlabeled containers of an image, for taking over from another manager. Docker is reached over its socket API directly; there's no Docker SDK dependency.

title: Docker
heading: Status
text: Tested against a real Docker daemon, with upstream PocketBase 0.23 and PocketOne 0.0.1 side by side, alone and as a host's runtime. Not yet in production. go test ./... runs the Docker tests when a daemon is reachable (they're skipped with -short ). The first run downloads an upstream release and a PocketOne release into the user cache.

title: Edge
text: The fleet layer for a Host: several servers (edges) share one set of instances, any edge accepts any request, and a request for an instance another edge runs is forwarded there over the private network. Works with either runtime provider, pocker or docker. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Edge
heading: Install
text: Edge is built into pocketone . It turns on in host mode (a provider in pocketone.yaml ) when the file has an edges section, or a mothership section (Mothership), which lists the edges too. In your own Go build, give the host a router as its forward hook: edges, err := edge.FromSection(log) // the edges section; nil when there is none if edges != nil { opts.Forward = edge.NewRouter(edge.RouterConfig{Edges: edges, Logger: log}).Forward } h, err := host.FromConfig(opts) The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/edge .

title: Edge
heading: Configure
text: The edges section names this edge and lists the others (keys below): edges: self: lax-1 list: { id: sgp-1, internal_url: "http://10.88.0.4:8080", region: sgp } server: plain: [":8080"] # where the other edges reach this one (their internal_url for it) Each entry needs id and internal_url . An instance another edge runs names its owner in remote : instances: id: shop hosts: [shop.example.com] remote: edge:@sgp-1 # also accepted: edge:sgp-1, or sgp-1 Without a mothership, instances come from the instances file. With one, instances and edges both come from it; a fixed edges.list entry wins over the mothership's for the same edge.

title: Edge
heading: edges:
text: The fleet: this edge's id and a fixed list of the other edges (id, internal_url, region). self string This edge's id, such as lax-1. list list of object The other edges: id, internal_url (where this edge reaches it) and optional region.

title: Edge
heading: Use
text: There's nothing to run by hand. A load balancer sends visitors to any edge, and each request ends up on the edge that runs its instance: Owner healthy: the request is forwarded to its internal_url , with the original hostname. An edge is healthy when its source heard from it in the last 30 seconds, or else when it answers /_pocker/health (an edge the source marks offline never is). Owner briefly unreachable but healthy: requests are held and retried every 250 ms until it answers. Only requests without a body (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) are replayed after a failed connection. Owner down or unknown: a 503 with Retry-After: 10 , at once. Never bounced: a request another edge already forwarded is never forwarded again; it gets a 421. CORS: for an instance with access.cors_origins , the entry edge answers preflights and sets the only Access-Control-Allow-Origin the browser sees. Headers: where both edges set the same header (such as the firewall's rate-limit headers), the owner's wins.

title: Edge
heading: Works with
text: Host Edge fills the host's forward hook for instances with remote set. Pocker, Docker Either runs the instances this edge owns; an app already running here stops when its instance moves to another edge. Firewall The entry edge checks the peer and the instance's rate limits before forwarding. Mothership Its mirror is an edge source: it follows the mothership's list of edges and their heartbeats.

title: Edge
heading: Building on Edge
text: Edge sources. Implement edge.EdgeSource ( Self , Resolve , Edges ) to say where the other edges are; add Run ( edge.Runner ) for background work. YAMLProvider is the edges.list one; MultiProvider combines several, the first to resolve an instance's remote winning. Router. edge.NewRouter(edge.RouterConfig{...}) takes the health path, healthy window, retry interval and the 503 and 421 messages. Plug Router.Forward into host.Host.Forward . Timing. edge.WithMark(ctx) records which edge a request was forwarded to and when, e.g. for Server-Timing.

title: Edge
heading: Example
text: Edge has no example program of its own. The stock binary wires it up in examples/pocketone/multi.go , together with the mothership's edge list.

title: Firewall
text: Peer allow-lists, trusted proxies and client IPs, and per-IP and per-instance rate limits for a Host, with or without Edge. Every request is checked before an instance serves it or it's forwarded to another edge. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Firewall
heading: Install
text: The firewall is built into pocketone . It turns on in host mode (a provider in pocketone.yaml ) when the file has a firewall or rate_limits section; there's nothing else to install. In your own Go build, importing the package registers it with the host, with the same rule: import _ "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/firewall" Or build one in Go and add it to the host's gates, as the example does. A single app doesn't need it: stock PocketBase has its own per-IP rate limits and trusted proxies.

title: Firewall
heading: Configure
text: Two sections, both optional; either one turns the firewall on (keys below). firewall: allow_cidrs: [] # peers allowed to connect (empty = everyone) trusted_proxies: [] # peers whose client-IP headers are believed client_ip_headers: [CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP] trusted_clients: [] # client IPs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance trusted_client_headers: [X-Client-IP] # a trusted client names its end user: each user gets their own limits rate_limit_header_prefix: X-RateLimit rate_limits: # defaults for every instance ip_hourly: 1000 instance_hourly: 10000 ip_concurrent: 15 instance_concurrent: 250 file_weight: 0.1 # a /api/files request costs a tenth trusted: { ip_hourly: 5000, instance_hourly: 20000, ip_concurrent: 50, instance_concurrent: 250 } # off: true # no rate limiting The values shown are the defaults. In dev mode ( instances: { dev: true } ) rate limiting is off unless the file has a rate_limits section. A trusted limit is never lower than the normal one. Each instance can set its own limits and trusted IPs in its plugins.firewall settings; missing fields keep the defaults: instances: id: api hosts: [api.example.com] plugins: firewall: { rate_limits: { ip_hourly: 5000, instance_concurrent: 500 }, trusted_ips: [203.0.113.0/24] }

title: Firewall
heading: firewall:
text: Peers allowed to connect, trusted proxies and client-IP headers, trusted clients, the rate-limit header prefix. Turns the firewall on. allow_cidrs list of string Peers (IPs or CIDRs) allowed to connect; others get 403. Empty: everyone. trusted_proxies list of string Peers whose client-IP headers are believed. client_ip_headers list of string Headers read, in order, for the client IP from a trusted proxy. Default CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP. trusted_clients list of string Client IPs or CIDRs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance. trusted_client_headers list of string Headers a trusted client uses to name its end user's IP, so each user gets their own limits. Default X-Client-IP. rate_limit_header_prefix string Prefix of the rate-limit response headers. Default X-RateLimit.

title: Firewall
heading: rate_limits:
text: Default rate limits for every instance (per instance: plugins.firewall.rate_limits). Turns the firewall on. ip_hourly int Requests per hour from one client IP to one instance. Default 1000. instance_hourly int Requests per hour to one instance from everyone. Default 10000. ip_concurrent int Requests one client IP may have open on one instance at once. Default 15. instance_concurrent int Requests one instance may have open at once. Default 250. file_weight number What a /api/files request costs, as a share of a request. Default 0.1. trusted.ip_hourly int Requests per hour from one trusted client IP to one instance. trusted.instance_hourly int Requests per hour to one instance. trusted.ip_concurrent int Requests one trusted client IP may have open on one instance at once. trusted.instance_concurrent int Requests one instance may have open at once. off bool No rate limiting. The default in dev mode unless rate_limits is set.

title: Firewall
heading: Use
text: What callers see: Peers outside allow_cidrs get 403. Client IP: taken from client_ip_headers only when the peer is a trusted proxy; otherwise it's the peer. The app then sees that client as the request's IP, so PocketBase's logs and its own rate limits see the visitor. Over a limit: 429 with Retry-After and a message naming the limit and the IP. Every routed response carries X-RateLimit-{Ip,Instance}-{Hourly,Concurrent}-{Limit,Remaining} and X-RateLimit-{Ip,Instance}-Hourly-Reset (with your prefix), listed in Access-Control-Expose-Headers so browser code can read them. Long-lived responses (realtime) count toward the concurrency limits until they end.

title: Firewall
heading: Trusted clients that serve many users
text: A trusted client (process-wide trusted_clients , or an instance's own trusted_ips ) that serves many users, such as a server-side proxy or SSR app, sends each request's end-user IP in a trusted_client_headers header. Per-IP limits then apply to that user, still with the trusted limits; without the header all its users share one bucket. The header is ignored from anyone else, so it can't be spoofed to escape a limit.

title: Firewall
heading: Works with
text: Host The firewall is a host gate: it checks the peer, then admits each request before the runtime or the forward hook. Pocker, Docker Either provider; the firewall runs in front of both. Edge The entry edge applies the limits before forwarding. The owner edge's rate-limit headers replace the entry edge's, since the owner counted every request for the instance. Multitenant (planned) Will write each instance's plugins.firewall settings, such as its owner's trusted IPs.

title: Firewall
heading: Building on the firewall
text: Per instance. Write plugins.firewall.rate_limits and plugins.firewall.trusted_ips into an instance's settings (from the instances file or your own instance source). Go API. firewall.Firewall{Config, RateLimits} is a host.Gate you can add to Host.Gates yourself; NewFirewall(cfg) builds one ready to use. ClientIP(r) gives a request's client. firewall.SectionAdjust changes the settings read from pocketone.yaml before the firewall is built.

title: Firewall
heading: Example
text: The firewall in front of a toy host: only 127.0.0.1 may connect, at 100 requests an hour per IP. Run it from this folder with go run ./example --instances instances.yaml . // The firewall in front of a host: every request is checked (allowed peers, rate limits) before a toy runtime // answers. In a PocketOne binary the firewall turns on from pocketone.yaml's firewall / rate_limits sections; here // it is built in Go. // // go run ./example --instances instances.yaml package main import ( "context" "flag" "fmt" "net/http" "os" "os/signal" "syscall" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/firewall" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/host" ) type okRuntime struct{} func (okRuntime) Name() string { return "ok" } func (okRuntime) Serves(inst host.Instance) bool { return true } func (okRuntime) Ready() bool { return true } func (okRuntime) ServeInstance(w http.ResponseWriter, _ http.Request, inst host.Instance) { fmt.Fprintf(w, "hello from %s\n", inst.ID) } func main() { instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file") listen := flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.1:8090", "listen address") flag.Parse() fw := &firewall.Firewall{ Config: firewall.Config{AllowCIDRs: []string{"127.0.0.1"}}, RateLimits: &firewall.RateLimits{IPHourly: 100}, } ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) defer stop() h := &host.Host{Source: &host.YAMLSource{Path: instances}, Runtime: okRuntime{}, Gates: []host.Gate{fw}, Listeners: host.Listeners{Listen: listen}} if err := h.Run(ctx); err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err) os.Exit(1) } }
