title: Pages
text: Server-rendered pages from a pb_pages folder, next to your pb_data . Each file becomes a route: EJS, Markdown, JSX and TSX templates, layouts, middleware and API routes, plus static files. Page code runs in your app's JS VM, so it can use your data directly. This is PocketPages v1, formerly the npm PocketPages package. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Pages
heading: Install
text: Pages is built into pocketone and on whenever a pb_pages folder exists next to pb_data . There's no switch: no folder, no pages. If the folder appears while the app runs, it starts serving it. In your own Go build, register it after the JS VM, since page code runs there: app := pocketbase.New() jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // page code runs in the app's JS VM pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{}) // serves pb_pages next to pb_data pages.RegisterCommand(app.RootCmd) // the pages create and pages starters commands app.Start() The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pages . See example/main.go and Create your own plugin.

title: Pages
heading: Where the folder is
text: By default the folder is pb_pages next to pb_data . To use another one: pocketone serve --pagesDir /path/to/pb_pages A relative path resolves against the working directory, like --hooksDir . Pages has no pocketone.yaml section.

title: Pages
heading: +config.js
text: Settings for your pages live in the folder itself, in pb_pages/+config.js : module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', require('./_private/datastar.js')], debug: false, } plugins [] Built-in plugins by name ( auth , realtime ), or JS plugins such as the add-ons. EJS and Markdown are always on. debug false Detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output even outside dev mode. +config.js runs on each page request. Unknown keys, unknown built-in names or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error, and the reason goes to the log.

title: Pages
heading: Dev mode
text: When the app runs in dev mode ( --dev , or app.dev in pocketone.yaml ), or +config.js sets debug: true , you get detailed error pages with the file and line, and ctx.log.debug output. Otherwise visitors see a plain "Something went wrong" page and the full error goes to the log.

title: Pages
heading: Start from a starter kit
text: pocketone pages starters # list the kits pocketone pages create myapp --starter daisyui-docs cd myapp pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. pages create makes a new folder (it must not exist yet) with pb_pages and anything the kit needs beside it, such as pb_migrations . Without --starter you get minimal . minimal One page, no layout, no build step (the default). mvp One page styled with MVP.css. htmx A realtime chat and counter with htmx and the realtime plugin. daisyui A navbar and drawer layout with Tailwind CSS and DaisyUI. daisyui-docs A docs site from Markdown pages. datastar A realtime chat with rooms, with Datastar. auth Sign-up, sign-in (password, OTP, OAuth2, anonymous), email flows and a protected account page.

title: Pages
heading: Write pages
text: Add or edit files in pb_pages and reload the browser; no restart is needed. A few examples of what the folder holds: pb_pages/ +config.js settings (above) +layout.ejs wraps every page +error.ejs your error page index.ejs / about.md /about blog/[slug].ejs /blog/anything feeds/rss/+api.js /feeds/rss, a route without a template _private/ partials, never served assets/app.css a static file The full contract is in SPEC.md: routes and precedence, middleware, +page.js and +api.js , EJS, partials, slots and layouts, Markdown, JSX and TSX, the ctx object, errors, the built-in auth and realtime plugins, JS plugins, add-ons and the changes from 0.x. Highlights: Static files get ETags and fingerprinted URLs through asset() . ctx.pb() is the bundled PocketBase JS SDK, called in-process as the visitor. ctx.res.sse() streams server-sent events. The auth plugin gives cookie sessions on PocketBase auth: password, OTP, anonymous, register, OAuth2 and the email flows (verification, password reset, email change). Accounts that need MFA can't sign in through pages yet.

title: Pages
heading: What you'll see in the log
text: Problems in the folder (a bad file name, two files claiming the same route) are logged as pages: ... errors. If the site served cleanly before, pages keeps the previous routes until the folder builds cleanly again. Errors thrown by page code are logged in full.

title: Pages
heading: Try the demo
text: example/ is a demo app with EJS, Markdown, JSX, auth, ctx.pb() , SSE and a JSON route. It has a live speed check at /speed . cd example && go run . serve --dir=./pb_data

title: Pages
heading: Works with
text: Pocker pockerplugin serves each instance's own pb_pages (below). OAuth Server Renders its sign-in screens from pb_pages/_private/oauth/ when you have them there ( pocketone oauth eject writes them). Deploy pb_pages deploys with your other pb_ folders. pull doesn't fetch it by default; name it: pocketone pull prod pb_pages . JS Errors Both run in the same JS VM; JS Errors covers pb_hooks , pages report their own file and line.

title: Pages
heading: Under pocker
text: pockerplugin.New(pages.Config{}) serves every instance's /pb_pages : srv := &pocker.Server{Config: cfg, Plugins: []pocker.Plugin{pockerplugin.New(pages.Config{})}} The stock pocketone binary doesn't add it in multi-instance mode yet; a custom build does, as above. Each start of an instance's app gets its own route table, compiled templates and caches. An instance that sleeps drops them; nothing is shared between instances. Page code runs in the instance's own sandboxed JS runtimes, under its limits (execution time, single allocations, call stack). include , require , ctx.resolve , ctx.res.file and asset never reach outside the instance's pb_pages ; $os file access stays inside the instance folder. Tests: pockerplugin_test.go. An instance turns pages off in its settings with plugins: { pages: { enabled: false } } . It's its own package (pockerplugin), so single-app builds don't link pocker. Measured (same machine as Speed, docs kit): each awake instance adds about 2.3 MB (50 instances: 41 MB idle to 155 MB). One instance under pocker serves about 4,000 requests/s (p50 5.6 ms, p99 80 ms at 50 concurrent): less than a single app because pocker keeps 2 prewarmed JS runtimes per instance ( hooks_pool_size ; a single app has 15) and every call goes through the sandbox. To try it: copy sites into pockerplugin/example/pb_root/ .localhost/pb_pages , run go run ./pockerplugin/example , and open http:// .localhost:8791 .

title: Pages
heading: Building on pages
text: Render a template from Go. pages.For(app).RenderTemplate(e, "oauth/signin", status, data) renders pb_pages/_private/oauth/signin.ejs (or .md , .jsx , .tsx ) as the whole response, with data as ctx.data and no middleware, layouts or +page.js , for any method. It returns handled=false when the project has no such template. OAuth Server uses it. Read the routes. pages.For(app) returns the service: Dir() is the folder, Table() the current route table, Errors() the problems from the last build. JS plugins. A factory in +config.js can add to ctx , run on each request and transform rendered HTML (SPEC.md, section 9.2). Add-ons are built this way.

title: Pages
heading: Example
text: example/main.go serves the demo in example/pb_pages : EJS, Markdown, JSX/TSX, auth, SSE and a JSON route. Run go run . serve --dir=./pb_data in example/ and open http://127.0.0.1:8090. // Command example runs one PocketBase app that serves the demo in ./pb_pages (EJS, Markdown, JSX/TSX, auth, // ctx.pb(), SSE, a JSON route, +404). ./pb_migrations creates a "notes" collection // with three seed notes. From this folder: // // go run . serve --dir=./pb_data // // Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. Edit anything in pb_pages and reload; no restart needed. // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / // password. package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/plugins/jsvm" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pages" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // page code runs in the app's JS VM pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{}) if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Pages
heading: Speed
text: ext/pages against npm PocketPages 0.22.5 (the last 0.x release), serving the same starter kit pages: the 0.x kits in pb_hooks/pages on stock PocketBase 0.41.1, the v1 ports in pb_pages on the PocketOne binary. minimal / (EJS) npm 0.22.5 620 30 ms 670 ms 5.7 ms ext/pages 10,850 1.8 ms 37 ms 0.2 ms daisyui-docs /docs/overview (layouts, Markdown, partial) npm 0.22.5 580 28 ms 1.1 s 6.5 ms ext/pages 6,510 4.1 ms 49 ms 0.4 ms PocketBase's own /api/health (the ceiling) PocketOne 55,000 0.9 ms 2.4 ms 0.1 ms About 17.5× more requests per second on the simple page and 11× on the docs page, with p99 latency 20× lower. Single requests take 0.2 to 0.4 ms instead of 6 ms. Memory after each run was similar (170 to 350 MB for both). Why: 0.x parsed routes, ran EJS through a JS implementation and loaded its plugins inside the JS VM on every request. v1 builds the route table once, compiles each template once (EJS to JS in Go, Markdown with goldmark) and enters the JS VM once per request. How it was measured (2026-11-11): Apple M1 Max, 10 cores, macOS 27, Go 1.27.4, hey against 127.0.0.1 . Each server was warmed with 500 requests, then hey -z 10s -c 50 and hey -n 2000 -c 1 ; two rounds, which agreed within 5%. Every response was a 200 with the full page. The 0.x docs kit inlines about 6 KB of CSS into each page where v1 links app.css . Rerun it with bench/run.sh : cp -R starters/daisyui-docs /tmp/v1-docs pocketone superuser upsert admin@example.com password --dir=/tmp/v1-docs/pb_data bench/run.sh v1-docs 8804 /docs/overview "$(which pocketone)" /tmp/v1-docs

title: PocketPages v1 specification
text: The contract for ext/pages , PocketOne's server-rendered multi-page app plugin. The test fixtures ( fixtures/ ), the starter kits and the PocketPages site are written against this document. Where the implementation and this document disagree, one of them is a bug. v1 is a clean API. It keeps PocketPages' ideas (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, middleware, private partials) and changes the shapes. Apps written for the npm package (0.x) don't run unchanged; "Changes from 0.x" (section 12) lists every difference.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 1. The pb_pages folder
text: Pages live in their own folder next to PocketBase's others: myapp/ pb_data/ pb_hooks/ pb_migrations/ pb_public/ pb_pages/ A single app finds it at pb_pages next to pb_data , or at --pagesDir (a relative path resolves against the working directory, like --hooksDir ). Serving is automatic: the standard PocketOne binary includes pages, and an app serves its pb_pages whenever the folder exists (it starts serving if the folder appears later). There is no on/off switch; no folder, no pages. Under the multitenant host every instance has its own pb_pages . If the folder doesn't exist, the plugin does nothing for that app. Page code can require() modules from pb_pages/node_modules , then from the app's usual module paths. The same require works in modules, JSX/TSX components and EJS templates: ./x and ../x are files in pb_pages , relative to the requiring file, never above pb_pages . Without an extension, .js , .ts , .tsx , .jsx , .json and .cjs are tried, then a folder's package.json or index . A bare name ( pkg , pkg/sub , @scope/pkg ) is looked up in the nearest node_modules folder from the requiring file's folder up to the top of pb_pages . A package resolves through its package.json : exports (a string, or conditions, where require , then node , then default are used), else main , else index.js . With exports , only what it lists can be required, and no entry may point outside the package. Anything not found that way goes to the app's own module loader. node_modules is never routed or served, and isn't watched: after changing files in it, change any file in pb_pages (or restart) to reload. Page code runs in the app's JS VM, so PocketBase's JSVM globals ( $app , Record , $dbx , $security , ...) are available, as far as the sandbox allows for untrusted apps. Deploying: pb_pages is part of an app's code, next to pb_hooks and pb_migrations (the deploy plugin uploads it the same way). Pages' own file access (routes, static files, includes, assets) never leaves pb_pages .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 1.1 Special names
text: A path segment (file or folder name) starting with one of these characters is never a URL: + Framework file: +config , +middleware , +page , +api ( .js or .ts ); +layout , +error , +404 ( .ejs , .jsx or .tsx ). One of each per folder. Any other + name is an error at startup. _ Private. _private/ folders hold partials and modules for include() and ctx.resolve() . Other _ names are ignored. - Ignored (drafts, notes). . Ignored (dotfiles). node_modules/ is never routed.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 1.2 Groups
text: A folder named (name) groups files without adding a URL segment: (marketing)/about.ejs serves /about . Groups can carry their own +layout.ejs , +middleware.js and _private/ .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.1 Pages
text: A page is a template file: .ejs , .md , .jsx or .tsx (4.5). index.ejs / about.ejs /about docs/index.md /docs (and /docs/ ) docs/routing.md /docs/routing products/[id].ejs /products/123 , with ctx.params.id = "123" [org]/[repo]/index.ejs /acme/web , with ctx.params = { org: "acme", repo: "web" } The extension is dropped. index maps to its folder. [name] matches exactly one non-empty segment. A segment may mix text and a parameter only as the whole segment; post-[id].ejs is an error at startup. A URL with a trailing slash matches the same route as without it. Pages never redirect to add or remove one. Matching is case-sensitive.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.2 API routes
text: A +api.js file serves its folder's URL without a template: feeds/rss/+api.js serves /feeds/rss . [param] folders work as for pages. If a folder has both +api.js and an index page, startup fails.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.3 Static files
text: Every other file is served as-is at its path (groups removed): assets/app.css serves /assets/app.css . Files that mustn't be served (build inputs such as a Tailwind source) take a - prefix: assets/-app.tailwind.css . Content type from the extension. ETag from the content hash; If-None-Match answers 304 . Fingerprinted URLs (see ctx.asset , 6.5) are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.4 Precedence
text: /api/... and /_/... are PocketBase's. Pages never see them, and a pb_pages/api/ folder is an error at startup. Among matching routes the most specific wins: compare segment by segment from the left; a literal segment beats a [param] . So products/new.ejs beats products/[id].ejs for /products/new . A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error). A URL nothing in pb_pages matches goes on to pb_public , then to PocketBase. If pb_pages/+404.ejs exists, a GET / HEAD that nothing (pages, pb_public , PocketBase) answers renders it inside the root layout with status 404 (never for /api/ or /_/ ). The root +middleware.js runs first; page code can still change the status. The route table is built when the app starts and rebuilt when anything in pb_pages changes. A rebuild never restarts the app or reloads pb_hooks . Startup errors (bad names, conflicts) are logged with the file path; the previous table keeps serving if there was one.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3. Request flow
text: For a URL that matches a page or API route, one JS call does all of this, in order: Plugins' onRequest (built-in and JS plugins, in config order). Middleware , root first: every +middleware.js from pb_pages/ down to the route's folder (groups included). Handlers : the folder's +page.js (or +api.js ): load , then the handler for the request method. Template (pages only), then layouts , innermost first. Response. The call runs under the app's usual JS limits (execution time, memory), as one unit. If any step sends a response ( ctx.res.redirect , json , html , text , file , sse ), the later steps are skipped.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3.1 Middleware
text: // pb_pages/admin/+middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') ctx.data.section = 'admin' return next() } One signature: (ctx, next) . Call next() to continue; return its result. Returning without calling next() ends the request. If no response was sent, that's an error (500, and in dev the error page names the middleware file). Share data through ctx.data .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3.2 Handlers: +page.js
text: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { ctx.data.product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id) }, post(ctx) { const { qty } = ctx.req.body() // ... return ctx.res.redirect( /products/${ctx.params.id} , { flash: 'Added to cart' }) }, } Exports any of load , get , post , put , patch , delete . A page that only renders but must accept a form post still needs post() {} : methods without a handler answer 405 . load runs for every method; then the method's handler, if there is one. HEAD runs load and get like GET (only the body is dropped), so keep side effects in post / put / patch / delete . A handler may set ctx.data fields, or return a plain object, which is shallow-assigned into ctx.data ( Object.assign ). There is no deep merge. A +page.js applies to every page in its folder. ctx.route.name tells them apart. A method with no handler still renders the page for GET and HEAD . Other methods without a handler answer 405 with an Allow header listing GET, HEAD and the methods that have handlers, in the order GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3.3 API handlers: +api.js
text: Same exports as +page.js . There is no template, so a handler must send a response; returning without one is a // pb_pages/feeds/latest/+api.js module.exports = { get(ctx) { const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20) return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) = ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') }))) }, }

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.1 EJS
text: Run JS, no output Output, HTML-escaped Output, raw Nothing Also remove the newline right after the tag Also remove whitespace before / after the tag on its line script server code Same as Escaping replaces & " ' with & < > " ' . null and undefined output as an empty string. A template is compiled once per content hash and reused. In scope inside a template: ctx , data (= ctx.data ), params (= ctx.params ), include , slot , asset (= ctx.asset ), meta (= ctx.meta ). A template returns its text. There is no echo ; anything you want in the output goes through a tag.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.2 Partials: include
text: include(name, locals?) renders a template from a _private/ folder and returns its text. Use <%- so its HTML isn't escaped. Lookup: _private/ in the current template's folder, then each parent folder up to pb_pages/ . For a template that is itself inside a _private/ folder, the search starts at the folder containing that _private/ (so its siblings are found first). A name starting with / looks only in pb_pages/_private/ . .. is not allowed. name may include its extension; without one, .ejs then .md are tried. The partial sees the same ctx , plus locals as top-level variables. Including more than 64 levels deep is an error (recursion guard).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.3 Slots and layouts
text: +layout.ejs files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every +layout.ejs from its own folder up to pb_pages/ , applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout. { % slot(name, fn) defines a named slot: fn 's output is captured and nothing is output in place. slot(name) returns a slot's content ( '' if not defined). slot() returns the content being wrapped: the page, or the inner layout. Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout. Defining the same name again replaces it; inside the new definition's fn , slot(name) still returns the previous content, so a layout can wrap it ( slot('title', () = { % Docs: <% }) ). Layouts are skipped when the response isn't HTML (a handler set another Content-Type ) or after ctx.res.layout(false) . A page with an inner extension gets that type: robots.txt.ejs serves /robots.txt as text/plain and feed.xml.ejs serves /feed.xml as XML, so layouts are skipped. .html (or no inner extension) is HTML. Page code can still set another Content-Type .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.4 Markdown pages
text: A .md page is EJS first, then Markdown (CommonMark + GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks). Front matter between lines at the top is YAML, removed before EJS runs. Each top-level key is passed to ctx.meta(key, value) , for pages and for included .md partials. Headings get id s: lowercased, characters other than a-z 0-9 - _ space removed, spaces to - ; a repeated id gets -1 , -2 , ... appended. Fenced code blocks render as " . Raw HTML passes through unchanged. Relative image paths go through ctx.asset . A .md partial is rendered (EJS, then Markdown) on its own and inserted as HTML; Markdown never runs twice on the same text. Leave blank lines around an include in Markdown so the HTML stays a block.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.5 JSX and TSX
text: .jsx and .tsx files are templates too: pages, layouts ( +layout.tsx ), +error / +404 , and partials in _private/ . They're compiled when first used by esbuild, which is built into the binary (no Node, no build step), and cached by content like EJS. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked. // pb_pages/products/[id].tsx import Price from './_private/Price' export default function Product({ data, slot }: any) { slot('title', data.product.getString('name')) return ( {data.product.getString('name')} ) } The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. Props: ctx , data , params , meta , asset , include , slot , children , plus an include 's locals. JSX renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration, no client-side React. Event handler props (functions) are dropped; use plain attributes ( onclick="..." , hx-get , data-on:click ). Text and attribute values are escaped. dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html }} inserts raw HTML. class and className both work, as do for and htmlFor . style takes a string or an object ( { marginTop: 4 } → margin-top:4 ). true renders a bare attribute; false , null and undefined leave it out. renders with in front of it (JSX can't write a doctype). In a layout, children is the inner content. slot(name) reads a named slot, slot(name, content) sets one (content is JSX or a string), slot() is the same as children . include(name, locals) returns the partial's HTML, ready to put in JSX. EJS can include a .jsx / .tsx partial: its locals become props. Components are ordinary modules: import Card from './_private/Card' (resolved like require , 3.2). Partials are looked up with extensions in this order: .ejs , .md , .jsx , .tsx . TypeScript modules. +page.ts , +api.ts , +middleware.ts , +config.ts and any .ts file reached by require / import work like their .js versions. A module whose only export is export default behaves like module.exports = ... .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 5. Responses
text: A handler or middleware sent one That one Page rendered 200 text/html; charset=utf-8 (or the status set with ctx.res.status ) HEAD As GET , without a body Handler for another method missing 405 + Allow Error thrown 500 (see 8) JSON is only sent through ctx.res.json (or +api.js ). Template output is never parsed as JSON.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6. The ctx object
text: One object per request, passed to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.1 ctx.req
text: method "GET" , "POST" , ... url { href, origin, pathname, search } query(name) First value of a query parameter as a string, or undefined query(name, { all: true }) Every value, as an array of strings query() { name: firstValue } for every parameter header(name) Request header, '' if absent cookie(name) Cookie value as a string, or undefined cookie(name, { json: true }) Cookie parsed as JSON ( undefined if absent or not JSON) cookies() { name: value } , strings body() Parsed body: JSON object, or form fields ( application/x-www-form-urlencoded , multipart/form-data ) as { name: value } (repeated names as arrays) files(name) Uploaded files for a multipart field, as PocketBase filesystem.File values ready for a record field ip Client IP as PocketBase resolves it (trusted proxy settings apply) event The underlying PocketBase RequestEvent , for anything not covered here Query values and cookies are strings unless you ask for JSON. Nothing is parsed for you.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.2 ctx.res
text: status(code) Status for the rendered page. Returns ctx.res . header(name, value) Set a response header; returns ctx.res . header(name) reads it back. cookie(name, value, options?) Set a cookie. Non-string values are JSON.stringify 'd; the value is then percent-encoded ( encodeURIComponent ), and ctx.req.cookie decodes it. Defaults: path=/ , HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , Secure when the request is HTTPS. Options: path , domain , maxAge (seconds), expires (Date), httpOnly , secure , sameSite . clearCookie(name, options?) Expire a cookie (same path / domain as when set). redirect(location, { status = 302, flash }?) Send a redirect. flash sets a one-time message (6.4). json(data) / json(status, data) Send JSON. html(html) / html(status, html) Send HTML as-is (no layouts). text(text) / text(status, text) Send plain text. file(path) Send a file from pb_pages (path relative to pb_pages ). sse() Start a text/event-stream response; returns { send(event, data, { id, retry }?), comment(text), close() } . layout(false) Render this page without layouts (e.g. an HTML fragment for htmx). sent true once a response has been sent.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.3 Data and routing
text: ctx.data Plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates. Starts as {} . ctx.params Route parameters, strings. Never includes query parameters. ctx.route { path, name, file } : the URL pattern without groups ( /products/[id] , /docs for docs/index.md ), the file name without extension ( [id] , index ; +api for API routes) and the file relative to pb_pages , groups included.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.4 Flash messages
text: ctx.res.redirect(path, { flash: 'Saved' }) stores the message as JSON in a cookie ( pp_flash , encoded like any cookie, HttpOnly , Max-Age=300 ). ctx.flash() on the next request returns it and clears it ( Max-Age=0 ). It returns undefined when there is none. Calling it again in the same request returns the same value. A flash can be any JSON value.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.5 Helpers
text: ctx.auth The authenticated record, or null . Set by PocketBase's own auth (an Authorization header) or by the auth plugin's cookie. ctx.app The app ( $app ): records, collections, settings. ctx.pb() A PocketBase JS SDK client (the bundled synchronous build) acting as the signed-in user ( ctx.auth ), or as a guest. Its requests go to the app's own API in-process (no network), so collection API rules, expand and field visibility apply exactly as for a browser. API errors throw the SDK's ClientResponseError ( e.status , e.response ). Only /api/ routes; file uploads through the SDK aren't supported (use ctx.app ). ctx.env(name) Environment variable, '' if unset (the app's environment; under the sandbox, the instance's). ctx.log debug , info , warn , error : to the app's log. debug only shows in dev. ctx.meta(key, value?) Per-request key/value store for page metadata (title, description). Set with two arguments, read with one. ctx.asset(path) URL for a static file in pb_pages , with its content hash: asset('app.css') → /assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css . Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; / -paths from pb_pages . A path that isn't a file in pb_pages is returned unchanged. ctx.include(name, locals?) Render a _private/ partial from JS (handlers, middleware, plugins) and get its text; same lookup as the template include , from the route's folder. ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?) Load a module from _private/ (same lookup as include ; without an extension, the name, then .js , then .json are tried). Modes: require (default, the module's exports), raw (file text), script (text wrapped in ), style (wrapped in ). ctx.pagesDir The absolute path of this app's pb_pages folder, e.g. for listing files with $os.readDir . Read-only. ctx.store(name, value?) The app's in-memory store ( $app.store() ): set with two arguments, read with one. ctx.dev true in dev mode. Fingerprinted asset names carry the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: name. .ext .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 7. Configuration: +config.js
text: // pb_pages/+config.js module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', require('./_private/datastar.js')], debug: false, } plugins [] Built-ins by name ( auth , realtime ), or JS plugin factories such as add-ons (9). EJS and Markdown are always on. debug false Detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output even outside dev mode. Unknown keys, unknown built-in names and duplicates are startup errors.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 8. Errors
text: Anything thrown in middleware, a handler or a template becomes a 500 . Dev mode or debug: true : an HTML error page with the message, the file and line (template lines map to the .ejs / .md source), and the stack trimmed to pb_pages -relative paths. Otherwise: a plain "Something went wrong" page. The full error always goes to the app's log. throw ctx.httpError(status, message) sends that status (e.g. 404 , 403 ) with a plain page showing message . In a +api.js it's JSON: { "status": 404, "message": "..." } . A custom error page: pb_pages/+error.ejs renders for every ctx.httpError and every 500 outside dev mode, with ctx.error = { status, message } , inside the root layout.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 9.1 Built-in
text: Turned on by name in +config.js . auth : cookie sessions on PocketBase auth, without calling the app over HTTP. Every request: reads the pb_auth cookie, validates the token, sets ctx.auth (or clears a bad cookie). The cookie holds { token, record } as JSON (the JS SDK's cookie format), HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , Secure on HTTPS, lasting as long as the collection's auth token. identity arguments accept any of the collection's identity fields (email by default). ctx.session.authMethods({ collection }) → { password: { enabled, identityFields }, otp: { enabled }, mfa: { enabled }, oauth2: { enabled, providers: [{ name, displayName }] } } , as PocketBase's auth-methods API. ctx.session.register(email, password, { collection = 'users', data, verify = true, signIn = true }) : creates the record; sends the verification email when verify ; signs in when signIn . ctx.session.signInWithPassword(identity, password, { collection }) ctx.session.requestOTP(email, { collection, create = false }) → otpId . Always returns an id (unknown emails get one that never validates, as PocketBase does); with create: true a missing record is created first. ctx.session.signInWithOTP(otpId, code, { collection }) ctx.session.signInAnonymously({ collection }) ctx.session.requestOAuth2(provider, { collection, redirectPath = '/auth/oauth/confirm', redirect = true }) : stores state in a cookie and returns the provider's URL; with redirect it also sends the redirect ( ctx.res.sent ). redirectPath must be a path on this site. PKCE is used when the provider supports it. ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(state, code, { createData }?) : completes it on the redirect path (the state cookie carries the provider, collection and PKCE verifier; it lasts 10 minutes and works once). The sign-in runs through PocketBase's own auth-with-oauth2 endpoint in-process, so sign-up, account linking (to the signed-in account, if any), the anti-hijacking checks and onRecordAuthWithOAuth2Request hooks behave as in PocketBase. createData is extra data for a new record. Returns { token, record, meta } ( meta is PocketBase's OAuth2 meta, with isNew ). Accounts that need MFA throw an error: pages doesn't do MFA yet. Apple answers with a POST, so read state and code from ctx.req.body() there. On HTTPS the state cookie is SameSite=None so it survives that cross-site POST. ctx.session.signIn(record) : set the cookie for a record you authenticated yourself. ctx.session.signOut() Email flows, with PocketBase's own checks and mail templates: requestVerification(email, { collection }) , confirmVerification(token) , requestPasswordReset(email, { collection }) , confirmPasswordReset(token, password, passwordConfirm) , requestEmailChange(newEmail) (needs ctx.auth ), confirmEmailChange(token, password) . Request methods never reveal whether an email exists. Every sign-in method sets ctx.auth for the rest of the request and returns { token, record } . realtime : PocketBase realtime from page code. ctx.realtime.send(topic, data, { filter }?) sends to every client subscribed to topic (the filter only narrows that set). data is always JSON-encoded (a string arrives as a JSON string, as PocketBase's own messages do). filter(client) returns true to include a client. client is PocketBase's realtime client: id() , get(key) , set(key, value) , hasSubscription(topic) . ctx.realtime.client(id) returns one client by id, or null . Sending never waits for slow clients: each message is handed to the client's queue in the background.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 9.2 JS plugins
text: A JS plugin is a factory that returns hooks: module.exports = (config) = ({ name: 'my-plugin', onRequest(ctx) {}, // before middleware extendContext(ctx) { ctx.hello = () = 'hi' }, transform({ html, ctx, file }) { return html }, // after each page or layout renders (not partials) }) config is the plugin's entry in +config.js when it's an object ( { factory, ...options } ), else {} . name is required and unique. There's no hook for treating other kinds of files as pages: a page's inner extension already does that ( robots.txt.ejs serves /robots.txt as text/plain , 4.5). Hooks run in config order. Every hook is optional. JS plugins run with the same permissions as the rest of the app's JS (sandboxed in a multitenant host).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 9.3 Add-ons
text: Plugins for third-party libraries ship as JS files in ext/pages/addons/ , not built into ext/pages . Copy one into pb_pages (usually _private/ ) and list it in +config.js with require . datastar.js (Datastar) adds ctx.datastar : ctx.datastar.scripts({ spa: { scope, selector }, realtime }?) returns the script tags ( spa turns on client-side navigation for links under scope , swapping selector ). With realtime: true the page subscribes to the datastar realtime topic and sets a $clientId signal to its realtime client id. ctx.datastar.patchElements(html, { selector, mode }?) , ctx.datastar.patchSignals(signals, { onlyIfMissing }?) ( signals is an object), ctx.datastar.executeScript(js) send SSE events on the current response. The first one starts the stream ( ctx.res.sent becomes true ); later steps still run, but their output isn't sent and the automatic patch below doesn't happen. The stream closes when the request ends. ctx.datastar.signals() returns the request's signals as an object (from the datastar query parameter on GET , the JSON body otherwise). mode is one of outer (default), inner , replace , prepend , append , before , after , remove . When a request has Datastar-Request: true , the rendered page (without layouts) is sent as a patchElements event, into Datastar-Selector if given. ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements(html, options?, { filter }?) , .patchSignals(signals, options?, { filter }?) and .executeScript(js, { filter }?) send the same events to datastar realtime subscribers (needs realtime ).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 10. Dev mode
text: On when the app runs in dev mode ( --dev ) or +config.js sets debug: true : detailed error pages (8); ctx.log.debug output; template cache keyed by content hash, so edits show on the next request (the route table is rebuilt on any file change in every mode).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 11. Starter kits
text: pocketbase pages create [--starter ] creates the folder (it must not exist) and copies the whole kit into it. Run it with cd && pocketbase serve --dir ./pb_data (PocketBase keeps pb_data next to its executable by default; pb_pages and pb_migrations are found next to pb_data ). pocketbase pages starters lists the kits. Kits: minimal (default), mvp , htmx , daisyui , daisyui-docs , datastar , auth . The command needs a build that includes ext/pages . It copies pb_pages/ plus anything beside it ( pb_migrations/ , README.md , a package.json for CSS tooling). Kits ship inside ext/pages ( starters/ ).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 12. Changes from 0.x (npm PocketPages)
text: pb_hooks/pages/ , booted by require('pocketpages') in a .pb.js pb_pages/ , no boot file, no npm install api object, re-spread into each call ctx with req , res , data , params , route , helpers Query parameters mixed into params , JSON-parsed ctx.params is route parameters only; ctx.req.query() returns strings Cookies JSON-parsed on read Strings; { json: true } to parse Middleware: return a value, or call next(extra) , chosen by arity (ctx, next) , data on ctx.data +load.js , +get.js , +post.js , ... per folder, results deep-merged One +page.js exporting load , get , post , ...; returned objects shallow-assigned Template output that parses as JSON is sent as JSON Only ctx.res.json or +api.js comments; layouts read slot / slots slot(name, fn) to define, slot(name) / slot() to read echo() writes during render Templates return text; streaming only through ctx.res.sse() redirect(path, { message }) puts the flash in ?__flash= ctx.res.redirect(path, { flash }) , one-time cookie, ctx.flash() asset() fingerprint: full SHA-256 First 12 hex characters +config.js plugins: npm package names, EJS options Built-in names or JS factories; EJS and Markdown always on auth plugin through the JS SDK over HTTP ( api.pb() ) ctx.session. , direct app calls url() , stringify() , micro-dash globals Removed: use ctx.req.url , JSON.stringify , plain JS pb() (js-sdk plugin over HTTP to localhost:8090 ) ctx.pb() : same SDK, built in, in-process, as the signed-in user Route with fewer segments could match a longer URL Segment counts must match create-pocketpages pocketbase pages create [--starter ]

title: PITR
text: Point-in-time restore: your database as it was at any moment in the last few days, restored from the dashboard. History is recorded with Litestream, next to your data or in an S3-compatible bucket. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: PITR
heading: Install
text: PITR is built into pocketone and on by default . Every app it serves starts recording history the first time it serves; there's nothing to install. To run without it: pocketone serve --pitr=false In your own Go build, register it before the app starts: app := pocketbase.New() pitr.MustRegister(app, pitr.Config{}) app.Start()

title: PITR
heading: On, off and how far back
text: Set it in pocketone.yaml : pitr: enabled: true # false turns it off retention: 72h # how far back a restore can go snapshot_interval: 24h # how often a full copy is taken Or with flags, which win over the file: --pitr true Record history while serving. --pitr=false turns it off. --pitrRetention 72h How far back a restore can go. A shorter snapshot_interval makes restores faster and uses more storage.

title: PITR
heading: Where the history is stored
text: By default the history is kept next to your database, in pb_data/litestream/ . That protects you from mistakes in your data, but not from losing the disk. To keep it somewhere else, use your own S3-compatible bucket: Open Settings → Backups in the dashboard and find Point-in-time restore . Tick Store the history in my own S3 bucket and fill in the endpoint, bucket, region, access key and secret. Tick Force path-style addressing for MinIO and similar servers. The prefix defaults to litestream . Click Test connection to check that the bucket accepts a write, then Save . From then on the history is recorded in the bucket, starting with a fresh copy, so restores go back to the moment you saved. The secret is never shown again after saving. If the app runs with an encryption key ( --encryptionEnv ), the secret is stored encrypted.

title: PITR
heading: pitr:
text: Point-in-time restore: on by default, retention, snapshot interval. The --pitr and --pitrRetention flags win. enabled bool On unless false. The --pitr flag wins. retention duration How far back a restore can go. Default 72h. The --pitrRetention flag wins. snapshot_interval duration How often a full copy is taken. Default 24h. Shorter: faster restores, more storage.

title: PITR
heading: What's covered
text: Your database: records, collections, settings and superusers. Not uploaded files, pb_hooks , pb_public or the logs database. Use PocketBase's backups for those. History starts with the first change after PITR is turned on, and goes back as far as the retention allows (72 hours by default).

title: PITR
heading: Restore from the dashboard
text: Open Settings → Backups . The Point-in-time restore section shows how far back you can go, how big the history is and where it's stored. Under Restore to , pick a date and time, then click Restore . The app keeps serving while the old database is rebuilt, then restarts with it. Only superusers see this section.

title: PITR
heading: Undo a restore
text: The database you replaced is kept in pb_data/litestream/before-restore.db , and history keeps recording, so a restore can be undone. After a restore, the section shows when you restored and to what time, with an Undo this restore button.

title: PITR
heading: From the command line
text: pocketone pitr status pocketone pitr restore --at 2026-11-11T14:05:00Z --to /tmp/then.db # a copy, any time pocketone pitr restore --at 2026-11-11T14:05:00Z # in place --at takes an RFC 3339 time. With --to , you get a copy of the database as it was, to inspect or pull records from; the app keeps running. Without --to , run it while the server is stopped: the restore is swapped in when it next starts.

title: PITR
heading: What it costs
text: About 176 KiB of memory per serving app, and the storage for your history. Replication runs only while the app is serving, never during CLI commands.

title: PITR
heading: Works with
text: Pocker Every instance on the host gets PITR. The pitr section sets the defaults for all of them; each instance can override enabled and retention (below). A restore restarts only that instance, and sleeping instances cost nothing. S3 Fallback Mount litestream on a backend and every app without its own bucket keeps its history there, under its own prefix. An app's own bucket (Settings → Backups) still wins. Multitenant (planned) Sets each instance's enabled and retention from its plan, for example a plan without PITR. PocketBase backups pb_data/litestream/ is left out of backup zips, and restoring a zip doesn't wipe it.

title: PITR
heading: Per-instance settings (pocker)
text: Each instance can override enabled and retention in its plugins.pitr settings, from instances.yaml or a provider: instances: id: abc plugins: { pitr: { retention: 168h } } id: free-plan-app plugins: { pitr: { enabled: false } } Each instance's history goes to instances/ /litestream/ in the shared bucket, or its own pb_data/litestream/ . A bucket in an instance's settings is refused, so credentials never sit in instance data.

title: PITR
heading: Building on PITR
text: Store history somewhere else. PITR asks PocketBase for a filesystem of kind litestream ( pitr.Kind ) through OnFilesystemCreate . Answer it and the history goes to your filesystem; S3 Fallback works this way. Set it per instance. Write plugins.pitr.enabled and plugins.pitr.retention into an instance's settings; PITR reads them when the instance starts. Multitenant will work this way. Go API. ( pitr.Plugin).Status(ctx, app) returns the restorable window, size, destination and last restore; Restore(ctx, app, at) restores an app to a time. REST API (superusers): GET /api/pitr for the status, POST /api/pitr/restore with {"at": " "} to restore.

title: PITR
heading: Example
text: example/main.go runs one app with point-in-time restore on, keeping three days. Run it with go run ./example serve from this folder. // Command example runs one PocketBase app with point-in-time restore: Litestream copies data.db continuously into // pb_data/litestream/, and Settings → Backups gets a "Point-in-time restore" section. // // go run ./example serve // go run ./example pitr status // go run ./example pitr restore --at 2026-11-11T14:05:00Z --to /tmp/then.db // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "log" "time" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pitr" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" pitr.MustRegister(app, pitr.Config{ Retention: 72 time.Hour, // on by default; Enabled: false turns it off // Bucket: &pitr.Bucket{Endpoint: "...", Bucket: "...", Region: "auto", AccessKey: "...", Secret: "...", Label: "EU"}, }) if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: PITR
heading: How it works
text: Go module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pitr , Litestream v0.5.18 (pinned). example/main.go runs one app with local history. Litestream continuously copies data.db to its destination: the app's own bucket (its PITR settings), else a filesystem of kind litestream (an OnFilesystemCreate handler, such as S3 Fallback), else pb_data/litestream/ . Buckets go through PocketBase's own S3 client, not the AWS SDK. Each LTX file's timestamp is kept in object metadata, so restoring to a time doesn't depend on upload times. Replication runs only while the app serves ( OnServe ), never for CLI commands. On terminate it's flushed and detached, so under pocker a sleeping instance costs nothing. A restore is built into a side file while the app keeps serving, then swapped in by app.Restart() . The replaced database is kept as pb_data/litestream/before-restore.db . Apps with different retention get separate Litestream stores, since Litestream applies retention per store. Cost per serving app: about 176 KiB of memory, 4 goroutines, 5 file descriptors. Binary: about +4 MiB.

title: Pocker
text: Many PocketBase instances in one process (like Docker, but for PocketBase), routed by hostname. Each instance is a normal PocketBase folder and starts on its first request, in tens of milliseconds. Pocker is a runtime provider for Host; its peer Docker runs each instance in a container instead. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Pocker
heading: Install
text: Pocker is built into pocketone . Name it as the provider in pocketone.yaml and pocketone serve hosts many instances instead of one app: provider: pocker In your own Go build, register it as a provider ( examples/pocketone/multi.go is the stock binary's version), or run a pocker.Server on its own as the example does: host.RegisterProvider(&pocker.Provider{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath, Plugins: []pocker.Plugin{ pitr.New(pitr.Config{}), // any PocketOne plugin, on every instance }}) The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pocker .

title: Pocker
heading: Configure
text: The pocker section sets where instances live, the JS pool, outbound network and the default limits for every instance (keys below). Listeners, instances and the firewall are the Host sections ( server , instances , firewall ). provider: pocker instances: { file: ./instances.yaml } pocker: root: ./pb_root # one folder per instance: / hooks_pool_size: 2 egress_allow: [] # private networks instances may still reach max_js_execution: 30s # default limits; each instance can override them max_js_allocation: 64MiB An instance overrides any limit in its own limits (missing fields keep the default): instances: id: shop hosts: [shop.example.com] limits: { max_js_execution: 60s, max_concurrent_js: 32 } Every instance runs the PocketOne code in the binary; an instance's version is ignored.

title: Pocker
heading: pocker:
text: Runtime provider pocker: instances run in-process (root folder, hooks pool, egress allow list, instance limit defaults). root string ./pb_root The folder holding one folder per instance: / . hooks_pool_size int 2 JS runtimes kept ready per instance (0: a new one for each hook run). max_js_execution duration 30s Longest any single JS call (hook, route, cron job, migration) may run. max_js_allocation int 67108864 Largest result a JS built-in may allocate in one step, such as 64MiB. max_call_stack_size int 2000 Deepest JS recursion allowed. max_sleep duration 10s Longest a JS sleep() call may wait. max_query_duration duration 30s Longest an SQL statement without its own deadline may run. http_send_max_timeout duration 1m0s Longest timeout a JS $http.send call may use. http_send_max_body int 10485760 Largest response body a JS $http.send call may read, such as 10MiB. max_concurrent_js int 16 JS calls an instance runs at once; more wait up to max_js_execution, then fail. egress_allow list of string Private networks (CIDRs) instances may still connect to. Default none: public addresses only.

title: Pocker
heading: Try it with any hostname
text: # pocketone.yaml server: { http: "127.0.0.1:8090" } provider: pocker instances: { dev: true } pocker: { root: ./pb_root } pocketone serve curl -H 'Host: blog.localhost' http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health # creates and serves ./pb_root/blog.localhost In dev mode a hostname no instance maps becomes an instance named after it, its folder is made on first use, and it runs in PocketBase dev mode. In production only the hostnames in the instances file are served (see Host).

title: Pocker
heading: Each instance
text: A normal PocketBase folder, / : pb_data , pb_hooks , pb_migrations , pb_public . Its dashboard is at https:// /_/ . Its JS hooks see only its own secrets , through $os.getenv and process.env . A change to its secrets , encryption_key , access , limits , dev , dir , superusers , private , plugins or remote restarts its app on the next request, after in-flight requests finish. A hostname change doesn't restart it. A change in pb_hooks restarts just that instance. A broken hooks file affects only that instance (below).

title: Pocker
heading: Broken hook files
text: In dev mode, a pb_hooks file that fails to load is logged and skipped, and the rest of the instance runs, so you can fix it live. Otherwise an instance doesn't start with a broken file. When a running instance's pb_hooks change, the new code starts beside the running app and takes over only once it has started. If it fails to load, the previous code keeps serving and the error goes to the instance log, so a bad edit never takes a working instance down.

title: Pocker
heading: Logs
text: PocketBase's own logs (the dashboard's Logs) are per instance, in its pb_data . console. from JS hooks goes to /logs/exec.log as JSON lines ( message , stream , time ), rotated to exec.log.1 at 10 MiB. A start failure is written there too.

title: Pocker
heading: Works with
text: Host Routing, listeners, instances file and gates. Pocker is one of its runtime providers. Sandbox Every instance's JS hooks, SQL and outbound network run in it, so one instance can't reach another or the host. Firewall Peer allow-list and rate limits in front of every instance; per-instance limits in plugins.firewall . Auto TLS In the stock binary: certificates for the hostnames instances map ( autotls section). Server Timing In the stock binary: Server-Timing headers on every response. Mailtrap In the stock binary: dev instances with SMTP off send mail to a local inbox. Edge Instances another edge runs are forwarded there instead of started here. Lifecycle Measures disk use and last request for each instance under root . PocketOne plugins In your own build, any plugin such as PITR, S3 Fallback or Mail Relay runs on every instance, and an instance's plugins. settings override the plugin's defaults. enabled: false turns it off for that instance.

title: Pocker
heading: Building on Pocker
text: Plugins. pocker.Provider.Plugins (or pocker.Server.Plugins ) takes any pluginkit.Plugin , registered on each instance's app before it starts with that instance's plugins. settings. Host-level code can implement Configurer , AppIniter , JSIniter , Starter , or a host Gate , Wrapper or TLSProvider . See POCKER.md. Setup per instance. SetupApp(inst, app) runs after migrations and before the app serves, e.g. to add a route checked against inst.Private . Manager. OnStart hands host code the Manager : WithInstanceStopped(ctx, id, fn) changes an instance's files while it's stopped (deploys, restores), StartInstance , Running , InstanceDir , LogInstance . Restarts. app.Restart() (PocketBase's backup restore, PITR) restarts only that instance.

title: Pocker
heading: Example
text: A Pocker build with one extension: a Go route and an admin dashboard page on every instance, in dev mode. Run it from this folder with go run ./example , then open http://blog.localhost:8090/_/ (login admin@example.com / password ). // Command pocker-extension is a Pocker build with one extension: a Go route and an admin dashboard page, // added to every instance. See docs/plugins.md. // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "context" "embed" "io/fs" "log" "net/http" "os" "os/signal" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/apis" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pocker" ) //go:embed ui var uiFiles embed.FS func main() { cfg := pocker.DefaultConfig() cfg.Dev = true // any hostname; drop this for production (instances.yaml required) ui, _ := fs.Sub(uiFiles, "ui") srv := &pocker.Server{ Config: cfg, // Runs for every instance's app after its migrations, before it serves. SetupApp: func(inst pocker.Instance, app core.App) error { // local testing: every instance gets superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" if err := devusers.Ensure(app); err != nil { return err } app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se core.ServeEvent) error { // a Go route, superuser only se.Router.GET("/api/hello", func(e core.RequestEvent) error { return e.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"instance": inst.ID}) }).Bind(apis.RequireSuperuserAuth()) // an admin dashboard extension: ui/main.js is loaded by the dashboard before its router starts se.UIExtensions = append(se.UIExtensions, core.UIExtension{Name: "hello", FS: ui}) return se.Next() }) return nil }, } ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt) defer stop() if err := srv.Run(ctx); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Pocker
heading: Untrusted instances
text: Pocker runs every instance's JS hooks in the sandbox. For why that's safe enough to host code from people you don't know, and where it isn't, see How is this safe?. Memory is the main limit: only one-shot allocations are capped, so a hook that grows memory slowly affects the whole process. POCKER.md lists what the sandbox covers.
