title: PocketBase docs
text: PocketOne doesn't change how PocketBase itself works, so its docs are the reference for everything outside the plugins. This site doesn't copy them. Introduction Collections API rules and filters Authentication Files upload and handling Working with relations Extend with JavaScript Extend with Go Going to production Web APIs reference PocketOne is built on PocketBase v0.41. When the docs there describe a newer release, some of it may not be in PocketOne yet.

title: What PocketOne adds
text: Run pocketone the way you run pocketbase . These are the differences you'll notice.

title: What PocketOne adds
heading: Point-in-time restore, on by default
text: Your database is replicated with Litestream, so you can restore it to any moment from Settings → Backups or with pocketone pitr restore . Turn it off with --pitr=false .

title: What PocketOne adds
heading: Mail you can see in dev mode
text: In dev mode ( serve --dev ), an app with no SMTP settings doesn't send through the system's sendmail . The mail is caught and shown at http://127.0.0.1:8025 .

title: What PocketOne adds
heading: Server-rendered pages
text: Put .ejs and Markdown files in a pb_pages folder and they're served as pages, with no build step. This site is one. pocketone pages create myapp starts a new site from a starter kit. Full docs are at pocketpages.dev.

title: What PocketOne adds
heading: A config file
text: Settings can live in pocketone.yaml , with secrets in a .env file beside it that your JS hooks never see. Without the file, PocketOne behaves like stock PocketBase. pocketone config lists every section, and pocketone config check checks a file. A full reference is coming to this site.

title: What PocketOne adds
heading: Commands for working with remote apps
text: pocketone login , remote and link : save logins to your apps. pocketone deploy , dev , pull and logs : ship pb_hooks , pb_migrations and pb_public to an app and watch it. pocketone upgrade : move to the latest release, keeping the old executable.

title: What PocketOne adds
heading: Agents and API tokens
text: An MCP endpoint at /mcp lets agents such as Claude manage your app and call its tools. Long-lived API tokens ( pbt_… ) with scopes, for scripts and integrations. Your app can act as an OAuth provider; pocketone login and MCP sign-in use it.

title: What PocketOne adds
heading: Everything else
text: Automatic TLS certificates, bulk mail to your own users, scheduled VACUUM, signed S3 download redirects, and more. See all plugins.

title: What PocketOne adds
heading: What stays the same
text: The admin dashboard, collections, rules, the REST and realtime APIs, JS hooks and migrations all work as in PocketBase. For those, the PocketBase docs are the reference.

title: Create your own plugin
text: A PocketOne plugin is Go code compiled into your build. It can add, to every instance: Go routes; PocketBase hooks; collections; admin dashboard screens. It can also run process-wide jobs and middleware.

title: Create your own plugin
heading: The plugin contract: pluginkit
text: Write a plugin once, against pluginkit (its own module, github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pluginkit ; core has no part in it), and the same value runs on a single app and on every instance under pocker: type Plugin struct{ cfg Config } func New(cfg Config) Plugin { return &Plugin{cfg: cfg} } func (p Plugin) Name() string { return "hello" } // config key, _hello_ collections, logs func (p Plugin) Register(app core.App, cfg pluginkit.Config) error { c := p.cfg if err := cfg.Decode(&c); err != nil { // this app's settings over the defaults (json tags) return err } app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se core.ServeEvent) error { / routes, UI extensions / return se.Next() }) return nil } // optional: a $hello global in the app's JS hooks func (p Plugin) BindJS(app core.App, vm goja.Runtime) { / vm.Set("$hello", ...) / } Single app: pluginkit.MustRegister(app, plugins...) , and pluginkit.BindJS(app, vm, plugins...) in jsvm's OnInit . The standard binary does this for the plugins it ships ( examples/pocketone ). Pocker: put the plugin in Server.Plugins . Pocker calls Register for every instance with that instance's settings (its plugins. ), over the defaults given to your constructor; process-wide settings come from a pocketone.yaml section your plugin owns ( pluginkit.NewSection ). enabled: false means Register and BindJS are never called for that instance. No pocker import: a contract plugin doesn't depend on ext/pocker, so single-app builds don't link it. Reach for the host interfaces below only for what's process-wide (a request gate, TLS, background jobs). Name the command with pluginkit.Command : when a message tells people what to run ("run 'pocketone login prod'"), build it from pluginkit.Command (default pocketone ), never a literal. A build shipped under another name (PocketHost's, say) sets it once in main , or with -ldflags "-X github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pluginkit.Command=pockethost" . bulkmail is the reference implementation. Status. pluginkit covers per-app plugins. The process-wide host interfaces below ( pocker.Server fields and Server.Plugins host interfaces) are pocker's for now; a pocketbase.Main(plugins...) entry point is planned. A complete, runnable example is in ext/pocker/example .

title: Create your own plugin
heading: Compiled in, not loaded at run time
text: Plugins are Go packages linked into the binary, the way Caddy modules work. Go's plugin package ( .so files) isn't used: it needs identical toolchain and dependency versions; it can't unload; it rules out static CGO_ENABLED=0 builds. A build is a small main.go that starts a pocker.Server with your code.

title: Create your own plugin
heading: Your module
text: PocketOne keeps PocketBase's module path, so upstream merges stay clean. Point it at PocketOne in your go.mod : require ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase v0.41.1 replace ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase = github.com/pockethost/pocketone Go only honors replace in the main module, so the final binary's go.mod needs this line, not only your plugin's.

title: Create your own plugin
heading: Per instance: Server.SetupApp
text: SetupApp runs for every instance's app after its migrations and before it serves. Bind hooks and routes there, as you would in a stand-alone PocketBase main.go : srv := &pocker.Server{ Config: cfg, SetupApp: func(inst pocker.Instance, app core.App) error { app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se core.ServeEvent) error { se.Router.GET("/api/hello", func(e core.RequestEvent) error { return e.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"instance": inst.ID}) }).Bind(apis.RequireSuperuserAuth()) return se.Next() }) app.OnRecordCreate("posts").BindFunc(func(e core.RecordEvent) error { // ... return e.Next() }) return nil }, } inst is the instance's config from the instances file or your provider: id, hosts and inst.Private . Private values are for your Go code only and are never visible to the instance's JS. Use them for per-instance tokens your plugin needs. If your plugin needs its own collections, create them in a migration or on bootstrap. Prefix them with _ _ so they never collide with the app's collections, and make them superuser-only unless they must be public.

title: Create your own plugin
heading: Admin screens: UIExtensions
text: The PocketBase dashboard loads extensions before it starts its router: Each extension is a named file system served at /_/extensions/ / . Every extension's main.js is bundled into /_/extensions.js . Add yours in the same OnServe hook: //go:embed ui var uiFiles embed.FS ui, _ := fs.Sub(uiFiles, "ui") se.UIExtensions = append(se.UIExtensions, core.UIExtension{Name: "hello", FS: ui}) ui/main.js runs in the dashboard with its UI kit ( t. ) and globals ( app.routes , app.store , app.pb ): // a new page, with a link in the header app.routes.superuserOnly("#/hello", async () = { const res = await app.pb.send("/api/hello"); return t.div({ className: "page" }, t.div({ className: "page-content" }, t.h1({}, "Hello"), t.p({}, Instance ${res.instance} )), ); }); app.store.headerLinks.push({ href: "#/hello", icon: "ri-emotion-happy-line", label: "Hello" }); // add to an existing screen: screens marked with pbEvent fire mount: with their element document.addEventListener("mount:pageBackupsSettings", (e) = { e.detail.prepend(t.p({ className: "txt-hint" }, "Hello from an extension.")); }); More hooks: app.store.settingsNavGroups adds entries to the Settings sidebar. Search pbEvent: in ui/src for every screen you can add to (Backups exposes pageBackupsSettings , backupsList , backupsSettingsForm , backupCreateModal and backupRestoreModal ). No build step: plain JS works. Bundle with Vite if you prefer. Experimental upstream: this UI extension API is undocumented and can change between PocketBase releases ( ui/README.md ). Keep main.js small, and test it after each upstream update.

title: Create your own plugin
heading: Process-wide: middleware, jobs, events
text: Server.Plugins Plugins: any pluginkit.Plugin (registered on every instance), plus host-only extras ( Configurer , Gate , TLSProvider , Wrapper , Starter ; see POCKER.md), e.g. pitr, storage, mailrelay, autotls, servertiming. Server.Wrap Middleware around every instance request, e.g. auth in front of all instances, metrics, headers. Server.OnStart Gets the Manager before the first request: start background jobs (schedules, sweeps) in your own goroutines. Server.OnEvent Instance events: started, stopped, restarted, failed. Server.Source Your own InstanceSource : instances from a database or control plane instead of instances.yaml . Server.Forward How requests for instances running on another server are forwarded. From the Manager , host code can: change an instance's files safely: WithInstanceStopped(ctx, id, fn) stops it, holds its requests, runs fn , then starts a fresh app; start it: StartInstance ; find its folder: InstanceDir ; write to its log: LogInstance .

title: Create your own plugin
heading: Rules for plugins that host untrusted instances
text: Your Go code runs with the host's full power, outside the JS sandbox: Act only for the instance you were called for. Use inst.ID and Manager.InstanceDir(inst.ID) ; never build a path from request input. Instance data needs instance auth. Protect routes that read or change it with PocketBase's auth middlewares ( apis.RequireSuperuserAuth() , record auth). Exposing something to JS is a sandbox decision. Expose a function to an instance's JS only if it's safe for a hostile tenant to call. See How is this safe?. Outbound calls follow the egress policy. Go's default HTTP client already refuses private addresses. If your plugin must reach a private service, give it its own http.Client and transport, and never let instance input pick the address.

title: Create your own plugin
heading: Contributing a plugin
text: Plugins are welcome, from us and from you. Open a pull request that adds ext/ / .

title: Create your own plugin
heading: Change PocketBase's core as little as possible
text: PocketOne stays close to upstream so every PocketBase release merges cleanly. If your plugin needs something the core doesn't offer yet: Add the smallest hook that makes it possible: an extension point or an override, not your plugin's logic. A nil-checked function field, a list callers can append to, or an event, with upstream behavior unchanged when nothing is registered. Make it generic. Name it for what it allows ("storage backend for an app"), not for your plugin. Assume someone else's plugin will use it too, and that we'll offer it to upstream PocketBase. Mark every changed line in PocketBase's own files with // PocketOne: and a few words on why, so the next upstream merge knows what to keep. Keep it separate: the core change goes in its own commit, with a test, ahead of the plugin. Prefer what exists: jsvm OnInit , OnServe , the record and request hooks, BaseAppConfig.DBConnect , UIExtensions . Many plugins need no core change at all.

title: Create your own plugin
heading: What a plugin folder contains
text: ext/ / go.mod module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/ README.md the plugin's docs, and its page on pocketone.dev (below) .go the plugin _test.go conformance_test.go the shared plugin test (below) example/main.go a minimal program that builds cleanly and shows the feature ui/ optional: admin screens (embedded main.js) example/main.go is required. Keep it as small as possible: just enough to build a binary that shows the feature working, with no extra harness. go build ./example and go vet ./... must pass with no warnings. ext/pocker/example and ext/sandbox/example are the size to aim for. Examples come with two logins: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com (verified, in users ), both with password password . Every example/main.go calls devusers.Register(app) right after pocketbase.New() (under pocker, devusers.Ensure(app) in SetupApp ), from ext/devusers . A fresh data dir is then ready to log in to, with no installer page and no CLI step. Never register it in a production build. conformance_test.go is required. It runs the shared plugin test from ext/pluginkit/conformance once: func TestConformance(t testing.T) { conformance.Run(t, func() pluginkit.Plugin { return myplugin.New(myplugin.Config{}) }) } It checks that the plugin registers, migrates, serves and shuts down on a fresh app with no goroutines left behind; that PocketBase's own collections are unchanged and every collection it adds is named _ or _ _… ; and that one plugin value serves several apps at once (as under pocker) without registering on one app touching another's hooks. A plugin that adds MCP tools ( ext/mcp ) also passes conformance.Options{Setup: ...} that registers MCP on the test apps; the test then checks each tool is named _ _ , is described, and has an object input schema ( pb_ is reserved). Run it with go test -race . It's the minimum every plugin passes; your own tests cover the feature. The README has five required sections , in this order. It is also your plugin's page on pocketone.dev. ## Install : how to get it (built into pocketone , or the lines to add to a Go build). ## Configure : the pocketone.yaml section, flags and settings screens. The site adds a table of your section's keys, generated from your pluginkit.NewSection defaults; describe each key with a doc:"…" struct tag. ## Use : day to day: the admin screens and what to click, the commands. ## Integrations : the plugins yours works with and how (pocker and multi-instance hosting go here, not in the sections above), and how other plugins can build on yours (hooks, filesystem kinds, per-instance settings, Go and REST APIs). ## Example : the code that uses it. A sentence on what your example/main.go runs, then the whole file in a differ. Without an example (a plugin built into pocketone ), say where to see it used. Write the first three for someone running one PocketOne app, not for a Go developer. Anything else (how it works, limits) goes in sections after these, and extra guides can sit next to the README as other .md files. Plugins here are MIT. The README ends with ## License and the single line MIT . A plugin under another license lives in its author's own repository, not here. Add your plugin to site/plugins.json and run cd site/sync && go run . to build its page. ext/pitr/README.md is the example to follow. CI enforces all of this. .github/workflows/plugins.yml fails when a plugin README is missing one of the five sections or its MIT ## License , or its Example doesn't match example/main.go , or when a module that implements pluginkit.Plugin has no conformance test, then builds, vets and runs go test -race on every module the change affects: the modules it touches, every module that reaches one of them through a replace , or all of them for a core change. Run the same checks locally from the repository root: go run ./.github/plugins check go run ./.github/plugins affected origin/main HEAD Tests that need an external tool (MinIO, Docker) skip themselves when it isn't installed, so they don't block CI. Dependencies stay in your module. Heavy libraries go in your plugin's go.mod , never in core's. Single app first. Where it makes sense, a plugin should work on one PocketBase app, and add more under the pocker (multitenant) host. MIT , like PocketBase and the rest of this repo. ## Planned plugins Our own plugins will live in this repo under ext/ , each as its own Go module ( github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/ ) with its own version tags. The list and what each will do is in ext/README.md.
